title: Blind Curvelet-Based Denoising of Seismic Surveys in Coherent and Incoherent Noise Environments
DAMA/LIBRA annual modulation and axion quark nugget dark matter model
other_family_note: particle detector (DAMA/LIBRA scintillator) event rates, theoretical modeling
rationale: Theoretical particle-physics proposal interpreting DAMA/LIBRA modulation via axion quark nuggets; no machine learning mentioned. DAS appears only as a possible future test, not analyzed.

title: Real-Time Train Tracking from Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: The abstract describes a tracking algorithm run on GPUs, with no machine-learning model mentioned. The authors analyze field DAS vibration signals from fiber cables beside railway tracks, using two installation types.

title: Fiber Optic Train Monitoring with Distributed Acoustic Sensing: Conventional and Neural Network Data Analysis
rationale: The authors apply neural network algorithms to recorded DAS data of an ICE 4 train, alongside conventional analysis, to track the train and count its cars. The data are observed field recordings from a commercial DAS system.

title: Fiber distributed acoustic sensing using convolutional long short-term memory network: a field test on high-speed railway intrusion detection
rationale: Authors apply a combined CNN and LSTM to multi-channel DAS signals from a real railway field experiment for intrusion detection and classification. DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: On the Broadband Instrument Response of Fiber‐Optic DAS Arrays
rationale: Authors compare field DAS recordings on a telecom fiber with a colocated broadband seismometer to estimate the transfer function; no machine learning is mentioned, only conventional calibration analysis.

title: Sparse recovery methodologies for quasi-distributed dynamic strain sensing
rationale: The work uses sparsity-based signal recovery, not machine learning. Experimental dynamic strain measurements come from a weak-FBG quasi-distributed acoustic sensing system, treated here as DAS data analyzed by the authors.

title: Heterogeneity of Seismic Wave Velocity in Earth's Mantle
rationale: This is a review of global tomography. The authors apply cluster analysis, a likely k-means-type classical ML step, to tomographic models; that is the only ML signal. DAS appears solely as a future data source.

title: Urban Seismic Site Characterization by Fiber‐Optic Seismology
rationale: The authors analyze ambient-noise recordings from the Stanford DAS array, using H/V ratios, Rayleigh-wave dispersion and joint inversion. These are conventional methods, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Noise Suppression of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on f-x Deconvolution and Wavelet Transform
rationale: Denoising relies on f-x deconvolution and wavelet transform, which are conventional signal processing rather than machine learning. Experimental DAS seismic-wave data were processed, implying observed data.

title: Fiber-optic distributed seismic sensing data generator and its application for training classification nets
rationale: The authors train a neural-network classifier on synthetic DAS seismic data they generate, then test it on experimental DSeiS field records. That makes DAS data central and partly observed, and the AI a method.

title: Technology Focus: Production Monitoring (March 2020)
rationale: Editorial feature summarizing other papers; ML early-warning system is described from a highlighted paper, not the authors' own analysis. DAS appears only in a recommended-reading title.

title: Detection and Quantization Technique of Optical Distributed Acoustic Coupling Based on φ-OTDR
Modeling the seismic response of individual hydraulic fracturing stages observed in a time-lapse distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profiling survey
rationale: Field DAS VSP data from a horizontal well recorded vibroseis P- and S-wave time shifts, analyzed with finite-difference elastic modeling and an effective medium fracture model; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Strain microseismics: Radiation patterns, synthetics, and moment tensor resolvability with distributed acoustic sensing in isotropic media
rationale: Analytical strain formulations and synthetic full-wavefield comparisons for DAS moment tensor resolvability; no machine learning mentioned. DAS is analyzed via simulated/theoretical data only, with no field observations.

title: Urban Near‐Surface Seismic Monitoring Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS recordings from the Stanford fiber observatory are processed with conventional noise removal and source normalization to track near-surface velocity changes from quarry blasts; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Microseismic monitoring using a fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensor array
rationale: Field downhole DAS microseismic case study using a simple detector and manual picking for event location, compared with a surface seismic array; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Integrating Distributed Acoustic Sensing, Treatment-Pressure Analysis, and Video-Based Perforation Imaging To Evaluate Limited-Entry-Treatment Effectiveness
other_family_note: wellbore treatment and surface pressure measurements (step-down tests)
rationale: The abstract describes no machine learning, only pressure analysis, video imaging and fracture simulation. DAS field data were analyzed to estimate how slurry was allocated among perforation clusters.

title: Axion Quark Nuggets. SkyQuakes and Other Mysterious Explosions
other_family_note: atmospheric infrasound array recording
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning. It interprets an observed infrasound array record alongside all-sky camera non-detections. DAS and seismic stations appear only as a proposed future detection strategy.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing for seismic activity monitoring
rationale: Perspective on DAS seismic monitoring presenting new experimental chirped-pulse DAS teleseism recordings and signal processing for ambient noise; no machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing of Seismic Properties in a Borehole Drilled on a Fast‐Flowing Greenlandic Outlet Glacier
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the authors analyze field borehole DAS vertical seismic profiles on Store Glacier, recording P and S waves, reflections and attenuation.

title: Gas pipeline leak noise measurements using optical fibre distributed acoustic sensing
Low-noise distributed acoustic sensing using enhanced backscattering fiber with ultra-low-loss point reflectors
rationale: The abstract describes building and testing a DAS phi-OTDR system on enhanced backscattering fiber, with measured phase noise. Acoustic strain sensing counts as seismic_elastic. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Detection-Localization-Identification of Vibrations Over Long Distance SSMF With Coherent $\Delta \phi$-OTDR
rationale: The paper proposes a coherent Δφ-OTDR DAS interrogation technique with experimental vibration detection over 50 km of fiber, compared against simulation. No machine learning is mentioned; localization uses a multi-resolution signal-processing approach.

title: Phase demodulation method based on a dual-identical-chirped-pulse and weak fiber Bragg gratings for quasi-distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The paper proposes a DFT-based phase demodulation method for quasi-DAS using weak FBGs and tests it numerically and in a PZT experiment over a 101.64 km fiber. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Design considerations for using Distributed Acoustic Sensing for cross‐well seismics: A case study for CO2 storage
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work uses rock-physics modeling and tomography design. DAS strain responses are modeled for cross-well survey design scenarios, and the abstract implies the data are entirely synthetic.

title: Rose Parade Seismology: Signatures of Floats and Bands on Optical Fiber
rationale: The Pasadena DAS array on telecom fiber recorded seismic signatures of floats and bands during the 2020 Rose Parade. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Coherent OTDR Using Flexible All-Digital Orthogonal Phase Code Pulse for Distributed Sensing
rationale: The abstract describes a hardware and signal scheme for coherent OTDR distributed acoustic sensing and mentions no machine learning. Experiments on a 15.4 km fiber recovered applied modulation waveforms, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: City‐Scale Dark Fiber DAS Measurements of Infrastructure Use During the COVID‐19 Pandemic
rationale: Vehicle detection uses template matching on roadbed strain from a dark-fiber DAS telecom cable, so no ML is involved. DAS field recordings are analyzed directly and compared with mobile phone location data and seismic noise levels.

title: Enhanced Optical Fiber for Distributed Acoustic Sensing beyond the Limits of Rayleigh Backscattering
other_family_note: optical fiber backscatter/attenuation characterization (laboratory photonics measurements)
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; engineered fiber characterization. The authors report DAS measurements with the enhanced fiber showing improved acoustic SNR, so DAS data were used. Fiber optical property measurements are coded as other.

title: Wave-equation dispersion spectrum inversion for near-surface characterization using fibre-optics acquisition
rationale: The authors process field DAS recordings of ambient noise and active-source data from a buried fiber in Saudi Arabia. Methods are similarity-weighted stacking and wave-equation dispersion inversion; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed optical fiber acoustic sensing method based on dual-chirped pulses and cross-correlation analysis
rationale: The paper proposes a phase-OTDR DAS method with an FBG array, demodulated by cross-correlation, with no machine learning. A lab experiment on 2 km of fiber with PZT-induced vibration gives observed DAS acoustic data.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing of microseismic sources and wave propagation in glaciated terrain
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning; the analysis locates events and studies seismic phases conventionally. Field DAS strain recordings from a fiber cable on a glacier surface are analyzed directly.

title: Variational Mode Decomposition-Based Threat Classification for Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: A linear SVM classifies VMD-derived statistical features from phase-OTDR DAS recordings of digging activities along a buried cable. These are observed field data, so this is ML applied to DAS data.

title: Large-scale multiplexed weak reflector array fabricated with a femtosecond laser for a fiber-optic quasi-distributed acoustic sensing system
rationale: The paper describes fabricating a femtosecond-laser reflector array and mentions no machine learning. A prototype quasi-distributed acoustic sensing fiber was tested, and its SNR was compared with plain single-mode fiber, implying measured DAS data.

title: Research Committee Update
rationale: A workshop announcement listing DAS and machine learning as topics; no data analysis is performed by the authors. DAS is central, but no data are analyzed, so DAS use is unclear.

title: Characteristics of microseismic data recorded by distributed acoustic sensing systems in anisotropic media
rationale: The study examines synthetic DAS microseismic recordings in VTI shale to characterize wave arrivals, shear-wave splitting and polarity reversals. It uses no machine learning, and all data described are simulated DAS strain.

title: Advancing Production Flow Profiling With Subatomic Fingerprints and Big Data Analytics
rationale: The title mentions big-data analytics, but the abstract never describes any ML model being applied. Smart chemical tracers with subatomic measurements are the data. DAS appears only as a costlier comparison technology.

title: SC-PSNET: A deep neural network for automatic P- and S-phase detection and arrival-time picker using 1C recordings
rationale: A CNN combined with an RNN is trained to pick P and S phases on synthetic and field 1C borehole recordings. DAS appears as one motivating 1C sensor type, but the abstract does not say the field data were DAS.

title: Fracture properties estimation using distributed acoustic sensing recording of guided waves in unconventional reservoirs
rationale: The authors analyzed field crosswell perforation-shot guided waves recorded on a DAS array and used simple geometric analysis to estimate fracture half-lengths. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: To: “Strain microseismics: Radiation patterns, synthetics, and moment tensor resolvability with distributed acoustic sensing in isotropic media,” Ismael Vera Rodriguez and Andreas Wuestefeld , Geophysics, 85 , no. 3, KS101–KS114, doi: 10.1190/geo2019-0373.1.
Application of machine learning to microseismic event detection in distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: The authors train the YOLOv3 CNN to detect microseismic events, using synthetic waveforms combined with real DAS noise. They then evaluate it on several field DAS data sets, so observed data are included.

title: Horizontally orthogonal distributed acoustic sensing array for earthquake- and ambient-noise-based multichannel analysis of surface waves
rationale: Field DAS array recorded ambient noise and an earthquake; the analysis uses MASW, noise interferometry and Monte Carlo inversion, all conventional methods. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Bandwidth-Enhanced Quasi-Distributed Acoustic Sensing With Interleaved Chirped Pulses
rationale: The paper presents a quasi-distributed acoustic sensing hardware scheme, Φ-OTDR with chirped pulses on a UWFBG array, tested in a proof-of-principle experiment measuring strain. Processing is matched filtering only, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Low‐Magnitude Seismicity With a Downhole Distributed Acoustic Sensing Array—Examples From the FORGE Geothermal Experiment
rationale: The authors analyze field downhole DAS records from FORGE, plus regional and surface seismic arrays, to detect, locate and cluster earthquakes. Template matching and clustering are described, with no machine-learning model named.

title: Frequent 4D monitoring with DAS 3D VSP in deep water to reveal injected water-sweep dynamics
rationale: Field time-lapse DAS VSP surveys in Gulf of Mexico wells were acquired and analyzed to track water flood; no machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Geophysical monitoring using active seismic techniques at the Citronelle Alabama CO2 storage demonstration site
An anti-noise ϕ -OTDR based distributed acoustic sensing system for high-speed railway intrusion detection
rationale: A phase-OTDR DAS system was deployed at a real railway station. Intrusion signals were classified with a ConvLSTM and CNN deep model, so the paper applies deep learning to observed field DAS data.

title: Repeat well logging using earthquake wave amplitudes measured by distributed acoustic sensors
rationale: Estimates near-well formation properties from earthquake strain amplitudes recorded on borehole DAS; no machine learning mentioned. Uses a synthetic example plus two field DAS datasets.

title: Introduction to this special section: Reservoir monitoring
rationale: Special-section introduction summarizing other papers; mentions 4D seismic, VSP, DAS logging and muon tomography only as topics of included papers, with no data analysis of its own. No AI is mentioned.

title: Self-copy-shift-based differential phase extracting method for fiber distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Signal-processing method for DAS phase demodulation (IQ, digital mixing); no machine learning mentioned. An experiment applying strain to the fiber shows DAS data were acquired and analyzed.

title: Chronic leak detection for single and multiphase flow: A critical review on onshore and offshore subsea and arctic conditions
Faseroptische Leckage-Ortung zum Nachweis von Undichtheiten in Bohrlochkomplettierungen
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) by fiber in borehole
rationale: Field DAS and DTS measurements detected nitrogen leak acoustics and temperature changes in a brine well; interpretation used a numerical acoustic simulation model. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Marine seismic observation by Distributed Acoustic Sensing using seafloor cable off Sanriku for long-term monitoring
Hydraulic frac-hit corridor (FHC) monitoring and analysis with high-resolution distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and far-field strain (FFS) measurements
Detection Method of Broken Rail Location Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Technology
rationale: Proposes an algorithm exploiting train-induced vibration propagation characteristics to detect broken rail locations; no machine learning mentioned. DAS vibration data measured on a test railway line were analyzed.

title: Sensing Earth and environment dynamics by telecommunication fiber-optic sensors: an urban experiment in Pennsylvania, USA
rationale: Describes deployment and calibration of a DAS array on dark telecom fiber, with observed seismic signals compared to seismometer and geophone data. No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis is preliminary signal inspection.

title: Fiber-Optic Seismology
rationale: A review of DAS seismology that mentions no machine learning. DAS is central, but the abstract summarizes prior applications rather than describing the authors analyzing their own data, so das_used is unclear.

title: The State of the Art in Monitoring and Verification: an update five years on
The Value of Information From Horizontal Distributed Acoustic Sensing Compared to Multicomponent Geophones Via Machine Learning
rationale: Authors trained a U-Net CNN with three-fold cross validation to classify reflectors in seismic images from 2D numerical experiments comparing simulated DAS and geophone data; all data are synthetic.

title: Multiparameter seismic elastic full-waveform inversion with combined geophone and shaped fiber-optic cable data
rationale: The work uses physics-based full-waveform inversion and radiation pattern analysis with no machine learning. Simulated 2D DAS and geophone data (Marmousi2 and simple models) are inverted, so DAS data are analyzed, all of them synthetic.

title: Modeling of fiber-optic strain responses to hydraulic fracturing
rationale: The study uses displacement discontinuity geomechanical modeling with no machine learning. It models low-frequency DAS and DSS strain responses and compares them with field data from HFTS-2, so DAS data are analyzed and some data are observed.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing as a Distributed Hydraulic Sensor in Fractured Bedrock
rationale: Field and laboratory experiments use DAS on borehole fiber to record low-frequency strain from hydraulic stressing. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned anywhere in the abstract.

title: Marine Sediment Characterized by Ocean‐Bottom Fiber‐Optic Seismology
rationale: The authors analyze 24 hours of ocean-bottom DAS ambient noise and earthquake recordings. Methods are dispersion inversion, f-k analysis and autocorrelation imaging. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Rock Deformation and Strain-Rate Characterization during Hydraulic Fracturing Treatments: Insights for Interpretation of Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic-Sensing Signals
rationale: The study relies on a physics-based hydraulic fracturing simulator and forward modeling, with no machine learning mentioned. It analyzes simulated low-frequency DAS strain rates in synthetic cases and interprets a field LF-DAS example, so observed data are included.

title: Comparison between Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Geophones: Downhole Microseismic Monitoring of the FORGE Geothermal Experiment
other_family_note: sonic logging (borehole acoustic velocity log) used for velocity model comparison
rationale: Field downhole DAS and geophone microseismic data at FORGE are compared using array processing, detection, location and magnitude estimation; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed fiber sensor and machine learning data analytics for pipeline protection against extrinsic intrusions and intrinsic corrosions
rationale: A phi-OTDR DAS system recorded acoustic waves along pipeline structures. Neural-network machine learning, both supervised and unsupervised, classified impact events and defects, with accuracies reported. The acoustic field sensed by DAS counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Near-surface characterization using a roadside distributed acoustic sensing array
rationale: Roadside DAS array records car- and earthquake-induced Rayleigh waves and quasistatic deformation. These are inverted for shear-wave velocity and Poisson's ratio using conventional inversion and a new objective function, with no machine learning. Geophone survey serves as comparison.

title: RETRACTED: Real Time Measurement of Airplane Flutter via Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors apply DAS fiber to sense mechanical vibration (flutter) on an airplane wing and report experimental results. No machine learning is mentioned. Structural vibration sensing by DAS falls under seismic_elastic.

title: Convolutional neural networks for automated microseismic detection in downhole distributed acoustic sensing data and comparison to a surface geophone array
rationale: A CNN is trained on synthetic events injected into real DAS noise, then applied to detect microseismic events in downhole DAS field data. Results are compared with a surface geophone array, so observed seismic data are used.

title: Footstep detection in urban seismic data with a convolutional neural network
rationale: Authors developed and tested a CNN that detects footsteps in labeled windows of field DAS recordings from the FORESEE telecom fiber array beneath Penn State campus, reaching about 84% test accuracy.

title: On the Detection Capabilities of Underwater Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Analyzes observed DAS records from three Mediterranean dark fibers alongside underwater and on-land seismometers, using spectral analysis and signal-to-noise modeling; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: IMPROVING THE TECHNOLOGY OF WORK OF MARSHALLING YARDS BASED ON REMOTE ACOUSTIC SOUNDING
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; video processing is a proposed program, not ML. DAS along rails is assessed with simulation and reflectogram methods, but whether field data were analyzed is unclear.

title: Horse Gait Identification Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS measurements of a buried fiber identify horse gaits and wave speeds; the abstract mentions no machine learning or AI method, only signal measurements and SNR analysis.

title: Surface-wave dispersion spectrum inversion method applied to Love and Rayleigh waves recorded by distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The inversion uses a genetic algorithm optimization and slant stack, not machine learning. The method is tested on synthetics and then applied to DAS active-source and ambient noise data recorded at a geothermal site.

title: Fibre-optic monitoring for high-temperature Carbon Capture, Utilization and Storage (CCUS) projects at geothermal energy sites
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. DAS is central: the abstract describes actual and planned deployments at two geothermal fields and practical considerations, but does not say whether any recorded data were analyzed.

title: Infrasonic, Acoustic and Seismic Waves Produced by the Axion Quark Nuggets
rationale: Theoretical estimates of infrasound and seismic signals from dark matter nuggets; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS appears only as a proposed future detection strategy, with no DAS data analyzed.

title: Take the Eh? train: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) of commuter trains in a Canadian City
Empirical Investigations of the Instrument Response for Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) across 17 Octaves
rationale: The authors estimate DAS instrument response empirically using transfer functions between DAS records and reference ground-motion data across several field experiments. No machine learning is mentioned, and the DAS data are observed.

title: On the phase fading effect in the dual-pulse heterodyne demodulated distributed acoustic sensing system
rationale: Analytical model of phase fading and a weighted-channel stacking algorithm, no machine learning mentioned. The method is validated with experimental DAS data, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Evaluating seismic beamforming capabilities of distributed acoustic sensing arrays
rationale: The authors compare DAS array beamforming against a co-located nodal seismometer array using recordings of a real regional earthquake. No machine learning is mentioned; beamforming is a conventional array-processing technique.

title: Surface seismics with DAS: An emerging alternative to modern point-sensor acquisition
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; the work evaluates DAS for surface seismic acquisition, supported by a desert field case study and synthetic examples, so DAS data are analyzed and at least one source is observed.

title: Case study of hydraulic fracture monitoring using multiwell integrated analysis based on low-frequency DAS data
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) by fiber
rationale: Field passive DAS (low- and high-frequency) and DTS data were acquired during fracturing in Montney and processed conventionally into strain maps; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Reciprocity-gap misfit functional for distributed acoustic sensing, combining data from passive and active sources
rationale: A physics-based full-waveform inversion with a reciprocity-gap misfit; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS strain data from earthquakes and exploration sources feed a pilot experiment, though whether the data are synthetic or field is not stated.

title: Hydraulic-Fracture-Width Inversion Using Low-Frequency Distributed-Acoustic-Sensing Strain Data—Part I: Algorithm and Sensitivity Analysis
rationale: Inversion relies on a Green function, least squares and MCMC, with no machine learning. Low-frequency DAS strain data are inverted; comparison with 'true' widths implies synthetic data, and field data appear only as background.

title: Validating the origin of microseismic events in target reservoir using guided waves recorded by DAS
rationale: The algorithm is physics-based, using dispersion curves to separate body and guided waves and measure their amplitudes, with no ML. It analyzes field DAS records above the Eagle Ford plus synthetic modeling and a surface-geophone catalog.

title: Long-distance distributed acoustic sensing utilizing negative frequency band
rationale: The paper presents a phi-OTDR DAS hardware scheme that uses the negative frequency band, demonstrated experimentally on a 103 km fiber measuring strain. The abstract mentions no machine learning.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing With Sensitivity-Enhanced Optical Cable
rationale: Hardware paper on a sensitivity-enhanced DAS cable tested in the lab and in a borehole VSP field test; DAS acoustic/seismic data were analyzed, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing of subsea wells
rationale: Describes a subsea DAS fiber topology and interrogation system, validated through laboratory and field trials, so DAS data were used. No machine learning is mentioned; the processing is spectral-based.

title: Using DAS to investigate traffic patterns at Brady Hot Springs, Nevada, USA
rationale: Field surface DAS array data at Brady Hot Springs are analyzed for vehicle signals. The workflow uses moveout analysis and velocity stacking only, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Introduction to this special section: Distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Editorial introduction to a DAS special section; no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central, but the editorial itself analyzes no data, and the summarized papers' data use is not specified, so DAS use is unclear.

title: Real-time hydraulic fracture monitoring and wellbore characterization with distributed acoustic sensing of pumping noise
rationale: A quantitative inversion workflow interprets DAS recordings of pump noise and is shown only on synthetic examples. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS acoustic data are central to the analysis.

title: Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Early Gas Detection in a Wellbore
other_family_note: surface gauge (pressure/flow) measurements in test well
rationale: Field DAS data from a 5000 ft test-well are analyzed with frequency-wavenumber processing to detect gas influx. No machine learning is mentioned. Surface gauge measurements are used for comparison.

title: Quantifying hydraulically induced fracture height and density from rapid time-lapse distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profile data
rationale: Rock-physics modeling and inversion of P-wave time delays from time-lapse DAS VSP field data in two horizontal wells, compared against microseismic results; no machine learning mentioned.

title: Utilizing distributed acoustic sensing and ocean bottom fiber optic cables for submarine structural characterization
rationale: Ambient noise DAS records from a Monterey Bay seafloor cable are processed with interferometry, dispersion inversion and migration. These are conventional methods; no machine learning is mentioned. The field DAS data are observed.

title: Quasi-distributed acoustic sensing with interleaved identical chirped pulses for multiplying the measurement slew-rate
rationale: Abstract describes a Φ-OTDR interrogation scheme for quasi-distributed acoustic sensing with a proof-of-principle strain-measurement experiment; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS (UWFBG-based Q-DAS) data are measured experimentally.

title: When Fracturing, Heed the Plugs
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (fiber-optic) and downhole casing inspection/diagnostic tool data
rationale: Trade article describing field observations of fracturing via fiber-optic DTS and DAS displays plus downhole casing inspection; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data were viewed during operations, though temperature data drove the key observation.

title: One Stage Forward or Two Stages Back: What Are We Treating? Identification of Internal Casing Erosion during Hydraulic Fracturing—A Montney Case Study Using Ultrasonic and Fiber-Optic Diagnostics
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS), distributed strain sensing, downhole pressure gauges, ultrasonic casing imaging, step-down pressure tests
rationale: Field case study in which DAS, DTS and DSS fiber data plus ultrasonic imaging and step-down tests diagnose casing erosion; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS data were analyzed in real time.

title: Testing of a permanent orbital surface source and distributed acoustic sensing for monitoring of unconventional reservoirs: Preliminary results from the Eagle Ford Shale
rationale: Field VSP test with an orbital vibrator source recorded on DAS in a deviated well; processing, repeatability and reflection imaging only. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: The sparsity of the response of a quasi-distributed fiber optic sensing system allows ‘overclocking’ its interrogation
Distributed Acoustic Sensing Vertical Seismic Profile Data Denoiser Based on Convolutional Neural Network
rationale: Authors propose and train a CNN denoiser for DAS VSP data, building the training set from field and synthetic DAS recordings; denoising results reported on DAS data, so DAS is used and data are not purely simulated.

title: Very broadband strain-rate measurements along a submarine fiber-optic cable off Cape Muroto, Nankai subduction zone, Japan
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DAS low-frequency signal interpreted as fiber temperature record)
rationale: Abstract reports field DAS observations on a submarine cable, compared with ocean-bottom seismometers, plus quasi-static signal treated as temperature sensing. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Deep Learning Based Threat Classification for Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using SNR Dependent Data Generation
rationale: CNN and fully connected networks classify DAS-recorded ground motion threats (hammer, digging). The training set is augmented from a limited set of real DAS signals using noise-based SNR generation, so observed data are used.

title: Real-Time DAS VSP Acquisition and Processing on Single- and Multi-Mode Fibers
rationale: The abstract describes a DAS VSP acquisition and real-time processing system with source synchronization and data formatting. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS seismic data acquisition is the core of the paper's own work, implying field data.

title: Rayleigh Φ-OTDR based DIS system design using hybrid features and machine learning algorithms
Fracture-Hit Detection Using LF-DAS Signals Measured during Multifracture Propagation in Unconventional Reservoirs
rationale: The study pairs physics-based fracture propagation simulation with handcrafted strain-rate features to detect fracture hits, with no machine learning mentioned. Simulated and field low-frequency DAS data are both analyzed.

title: Enhanced Temperature Measurement Performance: Fusing DTS and DAS Results
other_family_note: Fiber-optic temperature sensing: Raman DTS and DAS-derived distributed temperature gradient sensing
rationale: The fusion relies on Kalman filtering, which counts as classical estimation, not machine learning. DAS Rayleigh data are processed into temperature-gradient signals and fused with DTS, so DAS is used, but the sensed quantity is temperature.

title: Flow Profiling Using Fiber Optics in a Horizontal Steam Injector with Liner-Deployed Flow Control Devices
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) by fiber optics
rationale: DTS interpretation relies on shape language modeling (a spline fitting technique) plus a probabilistic approach, not machine learning. Field DAS and DTS data were used to monitor flow control device positions in the well.

title: Quasi-Distributed Fiber-Optic Acoustic Sensing With MIMO Technology
rationale: Quasi-distributed acoustic sensing with MIMO coding is verified through simulations and experiments; no machine learning is mentioned. QDAS is a DAS variant whose data are analyzed, so DAS is used and the family is seismic_elastic.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing Using a Large-Volume Airgun Source and Internet Fiber in an Urban Area
rationale: The authors recorded airgun wavefields with DAS on urban telecom fiber and compared them with geophones. Processing relies on stacking and signal enhancement; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Depth Constraints on Coseismic Velocity Changes From Frequency‐Dependent Measurements of Repeating Earthquake Waveforms
rationale: Coda analysis of repeating Parkfield earthquakes, with no machine learning mentioned. The authors support their depth interpretation with downhole geophone and distributed acoustic sensing observations, so DAS data are part of the analysis.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) for Natural Microseismicity Studies: A Case Study From Antarctica
rationale: Field DAS deployment at Rutford Ice Stream compared with geophones for detection, location, source inversion and shear-wave splitting; no machine learning mentioned, only conventional seismological methods.

title: Rotation, Strain, and Translation Sensors Performance Tests with Active Seismic Sources
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; this is a field sensor comparison. A DAS system was deployed in the active-source experiment, but the reported comparison centers on rotation rate sensors, so whether DAS data were analyzed is uncertain.

title: Humming Trains in Seismology: An Opportune Source for Probing the Shallow Crust
rationale: The paper applies seismic interferometry to train-generated tremors, with case studies in Canada and southern California, and mentions no machine learning. DAS appears only as a future dense-acquisition technology, not as data analyzed.

title: Downhole distributed acoustic seismic profiling at Skytrain Ice Rise, West Antarctica
rationale: Field DAS walkaway VSP in a borehole at Skytrain Ice Rise, with velocity and attenuation measurements and traveltime/amplitude modelling. No machine learning is mentioned; DAS data were recorded and analyzed.

title: Geomechanical Template for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Strain Patterns during Hydraulic Fracturing
rationale: The work uses a fracture simulator with finite element modeling, with no machine learning. Simulated DAS strain patterns were validated against observed low-frequency DAS data from HFTS2, so the data are not simulated only.

title: Rapid Response DAS Denoising Method Based on Deep Learning
rationale: Authors train an attention-based CNN to denoise DAS signals and evaluate it on real field highway data, so AI is the method and DAS data are analyzed; vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: On the comparison of strain measurements from fibre optics with a dense seismometer array at Etna volcano (Italy)
rationale: Field DAS strain recorded at Etna is compared with array-derived strain from 26 broadband seismometers. Only conventional array methods are used, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Recent Advances in Phase-Sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry (Ф-OTDR)
rationale: A review of Φ-OTDR/DAS development and the group's own progress. It mentions no machine learning. DAS is central, but the abstract does not say whether new DAS data were analyzed, so das_used is unclear.

title: Thermal Noise Limits for Optical Time Domain Reflectometry

rationale: The paper is an instrumentation demonstration of a DAS interrogator measuring phase/strain over long fibers, reporting noise and distortion figures. No machine learning is mentioned. The DAS measurements are the authors' own experimental data.

title: Towards Detecting Red Palm Weevil Using Machine Learning and Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing

title: Wireline distributed acoustic sensing allows 4.2 km deep vertical seismic profiling of the Rotliegend 150 °C geothermal reservoir in the North German Basin
rationale: The authors acquired field DAS vertical seismic profiling data in deep wells and compared it with geophone data. Processing relied on conventional filtering and stacking; no machine learning is mentioned.

rationale: The authors train GMM-based pattern classifiers on field ϕ-OTDR distributed acoustic sensing vibration data along a gas pipeline to identify machines and activities and to detect threats.

title: Partial discharge monitoring of cable joint based on fiber sensing technology
rationale: The paper builds a φ-OTDR DAS system with weak FBGs and records acoustic signals from a laboratory partial discharge. The data are measured, not synthetic. No machine learning is mentioned; analysis is signal detection of frequency, phase and position.

rationale: The work uses a physics-based propagator matrix method and dispersion inversion, with no machine learning. DAS field recordings of microseismic-induced guided waves from Eagle Ford are inverted, plus synthetic validation and a sonic log comparison.

rationale: Talk overviewing BAM's DAS applications for monitoring bridges, pipelines, railways and earthquakes, and showing results; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data from infrastructure monitoring implied as the group's own work.

title: Preliminary assessment of ship detection and trajectory evaluation using distributed acoustic sensing on an optical fiber telecom cable

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on Multi-Core Fiber
Application of improved time–frequency representation to local noise removal
rationale: The paper proposes a revised S transform with time-frequency filtering, a conventional signal-processing method with no machine learning. A real DAS VSP data example shows removal of fiber coupling noise.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Volcano‐Glacial Environments—Mount Meager, British Columbia

rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning. Phi-OTDR (DAS) and OFDR strain sensing were applied to a physical model wind turbine tower under vibration, so DAS data were analyzed as vibration/strain measurements.

title: High sensitivity and large measurable range distributed acoustic sensing with Rayleigh-enhanced fiber
rationale: Photonics DAS system using a signal-extraction algorithm and dechirping, with no machine learning mentioned. A proof-of-concept experiment measures strain on a 920 m Rayleigh-enhanced fiber, so DAS data were analyzed.

rationale: Purely analytical SPAC formulation for strain, rotation and tilt; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS appears only as a future practical application, and no data analysis is described, so seismic_elastic is the theoretical focus.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing for near-surface imaging using submarine telecommunication cable: A case study in the Trondheimsfjord, Norway
rationale: The authors recorded controlled-source seismic data on a seafloor telecom fiber with DAS and a towed hydrophone array, then processed the field data into images. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

rationale: The abstract describes no machine learning, only an active seismic source with waveform stacking. Field experiments used DAS measurements, including a seafloor cable, to track seismic velocity changes.

title: Seismic observation and subsurface imaging using an urban telecommunication optic-fiber cable

Recent advances in earthquake monitoring I: Ongoing revolution of seismic instrumentation

rationale: Field test of DAS cable coupling strategies compared with geophone recordings, using refraction and MASW analysis; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data analyzed directly.

title: Seismic Soundoff: How and why DAS succeeds
rationale: This is a podcast summary of a lecture promoting DAS for borehole seismology, with no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central, but the abstract describes no data analysis of the authors' own.

title: Road deformation monitoring and event detection using asphalt‐embedded distributed acoustic sensing (DAS)
other_family_note: OFDR distributed fiber strain and pavement strain gauges (static/quasi-static strain in infrastructure)
rationale: The authors embedded a DAS fiber in an asphalt test road and measured dynamic strain from traffic and pedestrians, validated with OFDR, strain gauges and FE modeling. The abstract mentions no machine learning.

title: Extracting high-resolution, multi-mode surface wave dispersion data from distributed acoustic sensing measurements using the multichannel analysis of surface waves
Monitoring and identification of wire breaks in prestressed concrete cylinder pipe based on distributed fiber optic acoustic sensing
Linking Distributed and Integrated Fiber-Optic Sensing
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; theoretical comparison plus field head-to-head comparison of DAS and integrated MFFI strain sensing on telecom fibers in Athens, so DAS data analyzed. MFFI integrated strain treated as seismic/elastic.

title: Research Progress in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Techniques
rationale: A review of DAS principles, fading and resolution solutions, and applications; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS is central, but as a review the abstract describes no data analysis of the authors' own.

title: Sensitive seismic sensors based on microwave frequency fiber interferometry in commercially deployed cables
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. A new fiber interferometer records earthquake strain, validated against seismic accelerometers and DAS interrogator recordings made in parallel. The DAS data are analyzed for comparison, not merely named.

title: Near-surface characterization using urban traffic noise recorded by fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors recorded urban traffic noise on a field DAS line, then applied seismic interferometry and Bayesian MCMC dispersion inversion. These are conventional methods; the abstract names no machine-learning approach.

title: 3D deep geothermal reservoir imaging with wireline distributed acoustic sensing in two boreholes
rationale: Field VSP data recorded with wireline fibre-optic DAS in two boreholes, processed with a standard workflow and Kirchhoff migration; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Surface Gravity Wave Interferometry and Ocean Current Monitoring With Ocean‐Bottom DAS
rationale: Analysis uses observed ocean-bottom DAS strain records near Gibraltar with cross-correlation, beamforming and waveform stretching; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS strain is classed as seismic_elastic.

title: CNN–Aided Optical Fiber Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Early Detection of Red Palm Weevil: A Field Experiment
rationale: Authors train CNN models on DAS recordings from a controlled environment and an outdoor farm to classify infested versus healthy palm trees. Field DAS acoustic data are analyzed directly, so DAS use is yes.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing in soil for infrastructure monitoring
rationale: Field study installing DAS fibre in different soils and comparing vibration response from impact tests via signal-to-noise ratio; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data are analyzed directly.

title: Fiber-Optic Sensing System Allows Real-Time Visualization of Gas-Kick Dynamics
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS), downhole pressure/temperature gauges, rig surface drilling data
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work visualizes fiber data. A full-scale test wellbore was instrumented with DAS and DTS plus P/T gauges, and the recorded data were analyzed, so DAS was used on observed data.

title: Digitalization of asset surveillance through distributed fiber-optic sensing: Geophysics and engineering diagnostics and streaming
rationale: Describes edge processing of DAS interrogator data streams, fast algorithms for diagnostics and event detection; no machine learning mentioned. DAS recordings are processed, implying observed field data from wells.

title: Time Synchronized Distributed Acoustic Sensing of Partial Discharge at the Oil-Pressboard Interface
rationale: Lab experiment: DAS records acoustic emissions from partial discharge and is compared with high-rate acoustic sensors and electrical PD measurements. Analysis relies on aliasing and phase-resolved PD analysis; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Using the three-station interferometry method to improve urban DAS ambient noise tomography
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; the work applies three-station noise interferometry and dispersion tomography to an observed urban telecom-fiber DAS ambient noise dataset, so DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Locating the Precise Sources of High‐Frequency Microseisms Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors analyze observed underwater DAS recordings off Valencia with a cross-correlation method to locate microseism sources. No machine learning is mentioned, and cross-correlation alone counts as conventional.

title: Deep compressed seismic learning for fast location and moment tensor inferences with natural and induced seismicity
rationale: A convolutional neural network, with an autoencoder as an alternative, predicts source location and moment tensor from compressed seismic records. DAS appears only as motivation about growing data volumes. Whether the data are observed or synthetic is not stated.

title: 4 cm Portable Active Seismic Source (PASS) for Meter- to Kilometer-Scale Imaging and Monitoring of Subsurface Structures
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; signal stacking of active-source chirps. Field deployment on a tailings embankment combined the source with a DAS array, recording seismic velocity and attenuation changes.

title: Geolocalization of Large-Scale DAS Channels Using a GPS-Tracked Moving Vehicle
rationale: The abstract describes no machine learning, only a geolocalization workflow. It analyzes field DAS recordings on roughly 100 km of dark fiber at Long Valley, using seismic signals from a GPS-tracked vehicle.

title: Microseismicity Monitoring and Site Characterization With Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS): The Case of the Irpinia Fault System (Southern Italy)
rationale: Field DAS recordings of local earthquakes and refraction experiments are analyzed with numerical simulations, amplitude correction and stacking. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Railway traffic monitoring with trackside fiber-optic cable by distributed acoustic sensing Technology
rationale: Six days of field DAS recordings from a 2-km trackside cable are analyzed with beamforming and peak counting to track trains. No machine-learning method is mentioned. Train-induced ground motion is an elastic signal, so seismic_elastic.

title: Denoising of distributed acoustic sensing data using supervised deep learning
rationale: Authors train a fully convolutional neural network to denoise DAS seismic data. They test it on both synthetic and real DAS recordings of earthquakes and microseismic events, so DAS use is yes and the data are not simulated only.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing time-lapse vertical seismic profiling during zipper-fracturing operations: Observations, modeling, and interpretation
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS vertical seismic profiling data acquired during zipper fracturing and support interpretation with 3D full-wavefield modeling. The abstract mentions no machine learning; the workflow is conventional seismic analysis.

title: Drone Detection and Localization Using Enhanced Fiber-Optic Acoustic Sensor and Distributed Acoustic Sensing Technology
rationale: The abstract describes a field test in which fiber-optic acoustic sensors are interrogated by DAS to capture drone sound. Localization uses acoustic field mapping and data fusion; no machine-learning model is mentioned.

title: Vectorial distributed acoustic sensing based on a multicore fiber and phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry
rationale: The abstract demonstrates a vectorial DAS system built on multicore fiber with phi-OTDR, reporting measured vibration and strain performance. It uses pulse compression signal processing only; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: High-precision distributed detection of rail defects by tracking the acoustic propagation waves
rationale: A fiber-optic DAS system records elastic waves along the rail in a field test. Defects are located with propagation fitting and a dual-frequency processing algorithm. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Fiber Optic Sensing for Surveillance of In-ground Long-term Storage (FOSSILS)
other_family_note: radiation detection via scintillation light transmitted through optical fiber
rationale: The abstract mentions developing smart algorithms for disturbance discrimination, but it never names ML. DAS is central, yet the testbed is still under construction, so no analyzed data are reported.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing: A New Tool or a New Paradigm
rationale: A theoretical overview and review of DAS technology, its limitations and applications; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS is central, but the abstract describes no data analyzed by the authors.

title: A deep learning approach for signal identification in the fluid injection process during hydraulic fracturing using distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: The authors train a combined CNN and BiLSTM network on DAS acoustic recordings and apply it to field data from a horizontal well, so DAS is used and the AI is part of the method.

title: Seismic Soundoff: What geophysicists and engineers need to know about DAS
rationale: Podcast discussing a DAS short course; no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central, but no own data analysis is described, so whether DAS data are analyzed cannot be determined.

title: Case study on amplitude and phase response comparison between DAS and 3C geophone VSP surveys at a test site in Japan
rationale: The abstract describes comparing amplitude and phase from field DAS and 3C geophone walk-away VSP data, plus a 1D model study and conventional imaging. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Monitoring Linear Infrastructures: Current Status and Trends
rationale: A review of DAS for railway, tunnel and pipeline monitoring that mentions no machine learning. DAS is the central topic, but the abstract describes summarizing case studies, not the authors analyzing DAS data themselves.

title: Evaluating Stimulation Effectiveness with Permanent Optical Fiber and Sealed Wellbore Pressure Monitoring: Bakken Shale Case Study
other_family_note: sealed wellbore pressure monitoring / cemented downhole pressure gauges
rationale: The field case study analyzes near-wellbore DAS, fiber crosswell strain, and sealed wellbore pressure data to assess fracture geometry and cluster efficiency. No machine learning or AI is mentioned.

title: Imaging near-surface S-wave velocity and attenuation models by full-waveform inversion with distributed acoustic sensing-recorded surface waves
rationale: Physics-based full-waveform inversion with the adjoint-state method and no machine learning mentioned. Field DAS surface-wave recordings from optical fibers at CaMI.FRS are analyzed directly, and geophones are mentioned as a comparison.

title: Sample2Sample: an improved self-supervised denoising framework for random noise suppression in distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profile data
rationale: Authors propose and train a self-supervised deep learning denoiser (Noise2Noise-based) on DAS VSP seismic data, tested on both synthetic and field data, so DAS is used and the data are not purely simulated.

title: Multiscale recurrent-guided denoising network for distributed acoustic sensing-vertical seismic profile background noise attenuation
rationale: Authors develop and apply an attention-based multiscale neural denoising network (RGSA-Net) to DAS-VSP records, tested on both synthetic and field DAS data.

title: Unpaired training: Optimize the seismic data denoising model without paired training data
rationale: Authors train a deep network with attention plus adversarial and cycle-consistent losses (CycleGAN-like) to denoise DAS VSP records, using synthetic and field DAS data, so AI is the method and DAS is used.

title: Understanding surface wave modal content for high-resolution imaging of submarine sediments with distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Ocean-bottom DAS data from a telecom cable off Sanriku are processed with seismic interferometry and dispersion-curve inversion, supported by simulations. The abstract mentions no machine-learning method.

title: Ensemble empirical mode decomposition and stacking model for filtering borehole distributed acoustic sensing records
rationale: Authors train a stacking ensemble of decision-tree classifiers (bagging and boosting style) on EEMD mode features to denoise borehole DAS seismic records, tested on synthetic and real DAS data.

title: Image-domain DAS 3D VSP elastic transmission tomography
rationale: The method relies on adjoint-state tomography and time-reverse imaging, with no machine learning mentioned. It is applied to an active-source DAS 3-D VSP field dataset from Alaska's North Slope.

title: Nonlinear Earthquake Response of Marine Sediments With Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors analyze observed DAS recordings of 105 earthquakes on an offshore Tohoku fiber cable, using autocorrelation functions to estimate velocity changes. No machine learning is mentioned; the methods are conventional signal processing.

title: Directional Sensitivity of DAS and Its Effect on Rayleigh-Wave Tomography: A Case Study in Oxnard, California
rationale: The study uses a field DAS array in Oxnard, ambient-noise cross-correlations and Rayleigh-wave tomography. These are conventional seismic methods, and the abstract mentions no machine learning.

title: Wave Equation Dispersion Inversion of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: Physics-based wave-equation dispersion inversion with no machine learning mentioned; the method is applied to synthetic and offshore field DAS strain-rate data, so DAS is used.

title: Fault Zone Imaging With Distributed Acoustic Sensing: Body‐To‐Surface Wave Scattering
rationale: Backprojection of DAS-recorded scattered wavefields from Ridgecrest aftershocks, compared against synthetic tests; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data analyzed directly.

title: Denoising of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Seismic Data Using an Integrated Framework
rationale: Denoising uses only conventional filters (bandpass, structure-oriented median, f-k dip filter); no machine learning is mentioned. The framework is applied to the observed FORGE geothermal DAS dataset containing earthquake and microseismic events.

title: Simultaneous distributed acoustic sensing and communication over a two-mode fiber
rationale: The work is an experimental photonics system in which DAS detects vibrations over a two-mode fiber alongside data transmission. No machine learning is mentioned. Real DAS measurements were taken in the experiment.

title: Sensing whales, storms, ships and earthquakes using an Arctic fibre optic cable
rationale: Observed DAS data from an Arctic telecom cable were used to detect whales, storms, ships and earthquakes. No machine learning is described; automated processing and fusion appear only as future directions.

title: Filtering Strategies for Deformation-Rate Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS data from trenched and surface-deployed fibers analyzed using 1D and 2D velocity-dip filtering; no machine learning mentioned, only conventional signal processing.

title: Acoustic Signals of a Meteoroid Recorded on a Large-NSeismic Network and Fiber-Optic Cables
rationale: Bayesian inversion of observed large-N seismic and DAS records of a meteoroid in Iceland; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data are analyzed directly, including a late arrival resolved by DAS.

title: Full-Waveform Inversion of Fiber-Optic VSP Data From Deviated Wells
rationale: Physics-based adjoint full-waveform inversion with no machine learning mentioned. The authors apply it to real DAS VSP fiber data from deviated wells and compare results against sonic logs.

title: Comparison of Raman, Brillouin, and Rayleigh Distributed Temperature Measurements in High-Rate Wells
other_family_note: Fiber-optic distributed temperature sensing (Raman, Brillouin, and Rayleigh/DAS-derived DTS) in wells, plus a laboratory thermocouple comparison
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work compares fiber-optic temperature methods. Low-pass filtered DAS data from wells and a lab test serve as Rayleigh DTS, so DAS data are analyzed, but the sensed quantity is temperature.

title: Optical Fiber Serpentine Arrangements for Vibration Analysis Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work uses FEM and reference sensors. A laboratory experiment applies DAS in serpentine fiber layouts to measure dynamic strain on an aluminum beam, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing in DFPS East Well
rationale: Dataset description of field DAS recordings from a well with a Fotech interrogator; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data are the release itself, implying acquired field data.

title: On the Use of Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data for In-Well Monitoring and Well Integrity: Qualitative Interpretation
other_family_note: Low-frequency in-well DAS strain response to temperature, pressure and flow (not an elastic wavefield)
rationale: The authors interpret observed low-frequency DAS data from tubing-clamped fiber for qualitative well integrity analysis. No machine learning is applied; automated interpretation algorithms are mentioned only as future work.

title: Evidence of Nonlinear Seismic Effects in the Earth from Downhole Distributed Acoustic Sensors
other_family_note: laboratory rock physics experiments on nonlinear wave combinations with saturating fluids
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis is spectral observation of nonlinear harmonics. Field vibroseis and orbital vibrator wavefields were recorded on a borehole fiber-optic DAS cable, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Partial Discharge Monitoring Technology based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing
Distributed fiber mountain seismic monitoring and steady-state analysis under natural earthquakes
rationale: A field test records natural earthquake waveforms on DAS and compares them with seismic stations. The analysis uses operational modal analysis, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Time-expanded φOTDR using low-frequency electronics
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; hardware paper on TE-φOTDR distributed acoustic sensing. The authors demonstrate distributed strain sensing over 20 m of fiber, which counts as DAS data analyzed experimentally.

title: Comparison of Amplitude Measurements on Borehole Geophone and DAS Data
rationale: The abstract compares field borehole geophone and DAS strain-rate amplitudes at the GeoLab site using calibration and differentiation. No machine-learning method is mentioned, and the DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Near-field target localisation based on the distributed acoustic sensing optical fibre in shallow water
rationale: A Φ-OTDR DAS fibre records underwater acoustic signals, and targets are located with a physics-based near-field spherical-wavefront principle. No machine learning is mentioned. The method is validated by both simulations and field experiments.

title: Comparisons Between Array Derived Dynamic Strain Rate (ADDS) and Fiber‐Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) Strain Rate
rationale: Direct comparison of observed DAS strain rate with geophone array-derived strain at PoroTomo for regional earthquakes; conventional signal processing only, no machine learning mentioned.

title: Characterization of Aquifer Poroelastic Response to Impulse and Oscillatory Well Pressure Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field injection experiments in an aquifer measured depth-dependent strain with fiber-optic DAS; well pressure stimulation implies hydrologic data. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Effect of Source Mispositioning on the Repeatability of 4D Vertical Seismic Profiling Acquired with Distributed Acoustic Sensors
rationale: Field DAS VSP experiments with vibroseis at Otway and Curtin sites assess repeatability under source mispositioning; no machine learning is mentioned, so the analysis is conventional seismic processing.

title: Development of a rapid and quantitative prediction model for assessing the leakage status of water pipeline systems
Measuring the thickness and Young’s modulus of the ice pack with DAS, a test case on a frozen mountain lake
rationale: Field DAS recordings of ambient noise and hammer shots on a frozen lake; dispersion curves inverted with a Bayesian scheme. No machine learning is mentioned. Ice thickness was checked against field measurements.

title: Urban DAS Data Processing and Its Preliminary Application to City Traffic Monitoring
rationale: A signal-processing workflow extracts slope and coherency attributes from field DAS recordings in Hangzhou, with video used for validation. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS traffic vibration counts as seismic_elastic; the video is treated as RGB imagery.

title: DAS Over 1,007-km Hybrid Link With 10-Tb/s DP-16QAM Co-Propagation Using Frequency-Diverse Chirped Pulses
rationale: Reports a DAS sensing experiment over field and lab fibers using chirped pulses, coherent detection and correlation; no machine learning mentioned. DAS strain measurements were acquired and analyzed, including a real-time FPGA implementation.

title: Time-Delay Estimation of Microseismic DAS Data Using Band-Limited Phase-Only Correlation
rationale: Signal-processing method (S-transform plus phase-only correlation) compared with cross correlation; no machine learning. Tested on synthetic and real microseismic DAS datasets, so DAS is used with observed data.

title: Efficient SPSNet for Downhole Weak DAS Signals Recovery
rationale: The authors design and train a neural network (SPSNet) to denoise downhole DAS VSP data. Training uses synthetic geologic models. The abstract does not clearly say whether field DAS records were also tested.

title: A Dual-Stage-Recognition Network for Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing Perimeter Security System
rationale: Authors apply a decision tree classifier and a BP neural network to classify intrusion events in DAS perimeter security data. A month-long field test is reported, so observed DAS vibration data were analyzed.

title: Background Noise Suppression for DAS-VSP Records Using GC-AB-Unet
rationale: The authors propose a U-Net variant with attention and global-context blocks to denoise DAS-VSP records. It is trained on synthetic data plus real DAS noise and tested on field DAS-VSP data, so observed DAS data are used.

title: From Coherent Systems Technology to Advanced Fiber Sensing for Smart Network Monitoring
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; the work applies coherent detection and digital signal processing to DAS over telecom fiber. DAS is central, but the abstract does not say whether data were actually analyzed.

title: Silixa Chief Expects CCS Boom To Create “Huge Opportunity” for Fiber Optics
rationale: Trade-magazine Q&A interview about fiber-optic business prospects in CCS; no ML mentioned. DAS is described only as company background and industry context, with no data analyzed by the authors.

title: Technology Focus: Hydraulic Fracturing Modeling (November 2022)
rationale: Editorial technology-focus overview; machine learning is mentioned only as a general trend, with no model applied by the authors. DAS appears only as a background calibration technique and a recommended reading, not as analyzed data.

title: Seismic Monitoring of Machinery through Noise Interferometry of Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS and seismometer noise records with noise interferometry, beamforming and NCF modeling, all conventional methods. No machine learning is mentioned, and DAS data are central to the analysis.

title: Seismic Noise Interferometry and Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS): Inverting for the Firn Layer S‐Velocity Structure on Rutford Ice Stream, Antarctica
rationale: Field DAS and geophone noise data on Rutford Ice Stream are cross-correlated and the dispersion curve is inverted for S-velocity. These are conventional interferometry and inversion steps; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Multi-scale interactive network in the application of DAS seismic data processing
rationale: Authors propose a multi-scale CNN (MSI-Net) and apply it to denoise DAS seismic data, tested on both synthetic and real DAS examples.

title: The Effectiveness of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) for Broken Rail Detection
rationale: Field tests of DAS on railway track to detect rail breaks, analyzed with gradient analysis and convolution techniques; no machine learning is mentioned. The sensed field is vibration/acoustic, so seismic_elastic.

title: Phase-sensitive distributed Rayleigh fiber sensing enabling the real-time monitoring of the refractive index with a sub-cm resolution by all-optical coherent pulse compression
rationale: Describes a new phase-sensitive DAS interrogator architecture with experimentally reported sub-cm resolution and real-time refractive index monitoring. No machine learning or AI is mentioned. DAS data from the built system are central.

title: Measurement of Gas-Phase Velocities in Two-Phase Flow Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
other_family_note: Conductance-based multiphase flow sensor used as the reference for gas-phase velocity in a laboratory flow loop
rationale: DAS fiber wrapped on a lab pipeline measures slug-flow gas velocity using k–f integration and cross-correlation, with no machine learning. Results are validated against a conductance sensor. The observed laboratory data give das_used yes.

title: Removing multiple types of noise of distributed acoustic sensing seismic data using attention-guided denoising convolutional neural network
rationale: Authors build and apply an attention-guided CNN (ADNet) to denoise DAS VSP seismic data, trained on synthetic forward models and tested on both synthetic and field DAS records.

title: PubDAS: A PUBlic Distributed Acoustic Sensing Datasets Repository for Geosciences
rationale: Dataset repository paper describing eight field DAS datasets (seismic wavefields, active source). No machine learning is mentioned. The DAS data themselves are the paper's subject and are described and shared.

title: Automatic classification with an autoencoder of seismic signals on a distributed acoustic sensing cable
rationale: Authors apply an autoencoder deep network and Gaussian mixture clustering to spectrograms of signals recorded by a borehole DAS array at FORGE during 2019 stimulation; observed DAS seismic data analyzed directly.

title: Speech signal enhancement based on deep learning in distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Authors build a complex convolution recurrent network to denoise speech signals that were recorded experimentally with a DAS system. DAS senses an acoustic field, so the family is seismic_elastic.

title: Simultaneous reconstruction and denoising for DAS-VSP seismic data by RRU-net
rationale: Authors develop and train a U-net variant (RRU-net) to reconstruct and denoise DAS-VSP data, tested on two synthetic datasets and one field dataset, so DAS data are analyzed and observed data are included.

title: Magnitude estimation and ground motion prediction to harness fiber optic distributed acoustic sensing for earthquake early warning
rationale: Analysis applies slant-stack conversion, a theoretical source model and ground motion prediction equations to DAS strain recordings of real earthquakes. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Traffic flow and vehicle speed monitoring with the object detection method from the roadside distributed acoustic sensing array
rationale: Authors train a deep learning real-time object detector (YOLO-style) on labeled images built from roadside DAS recordings near Beijing to detect vehicles and estimate speed. Field DAS vibration data count as seismic_elastic.

title: A Hydraulic Fracture Geometry Inversion Model Based on Distributed-Acoustic -Sensing Data
other_family_note: hydraulic fracturing injection rate (pumping) data
rationale: The inversion uses a Green function with Picard iteration and least squares, not machine learning. LF- and HF-DAS data feed the model, validated on a DDM-simulated fracture case. Whether field data were used is unstated.

title: Revealing the shallow soil structure of the Yigong Lake in the Tibetan Plateau using a portable distributed acoustic sensing interrogator
rationale: Field DAS ambient noise recorded on two fiber lines near Yigong Lake, processed with noise interferometry and MASW for shear velocity profiles; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Offshore subsurface characterization enabled by fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing (DAS): An East China Sea 3D VSP survey example
rationale: The authors process and image observed 3D DAS-VSP field data from the East China Sea with conventional denoising, deghosting, wavefield separation and Gaussian beam migration. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Accelerating the phase demodulation process for heterodyne Φ-OTDR using spatial phase shifting
rationale: The abstract describes an algebraic spatial phase-shifting demodulation method, with no machine learning. It is tested on simulated and experimental heterodyne Φ-OTDR data, which is the sensing basis of DAS, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Method of precise sensing channel positioning forϕ-OTDR-based DAS
rationale: Laboratory experiment with a DAS interrogator recording bending-element vibrations in sand and clay; analysis uses signal statistics (skewness, peak shift), with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Shallow Structure Imaging Using Multi-mode Dispersion Curves Based on Multi-window HLRT in DAS Observation
Denoising and wavefield separation method for DAS VSP via deep learning
Achievement and future prospects of the demonstration test of the DAS-VSP reservoir monitoring system using permanent seismic source（ACROSS）
rationale: Field DAS-VSP data were acquired at Aquistore with the ACROSS source and processed conventionally (signal processing, noise suppression, RTM). The abstract mentions no machine learning.

title: Investigation of the effects of surrounding media on the distributed acoustic sensing of a helically wound fibre-optic cable with application to the New Afton deposit, British Columbia
rationale: The paper builds an analytical model and compares it with COMSOL simulations; no machine learning is used. It analyzes helically wound cable DAS, including field data from New Afton, so DAS is used and the data are partly observed.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing recordings of low-frequency whale calls and ship noise offshore Central Oregon
rationale: The abstract describes collecting and releasing field DAS recordings on offshore Oregon cables that capture whale calls and ship noise. It mentions no machine learning; DAS data are clearly analyzed and shared.

title: Machine learning-assisted processing workflow for multi-fiber DAS microseismic data
rationale: Authors trained a CNN for event detection and a U-Net for P/S picking, applied to field multiwell DAS microseismic datasets from western Canada, with co-located borehole geophones used for comparison.

title: Intrusive and non-intrusive microflow measurement based on distributed optical fiber acoustic sensing
Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on Microtremor Survey Method for Near-Surface Active Faults Exploration: A Case Study in Datong Basin, China
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) and Brillouin optical time domain reflectometry (BOTDR) fiber strain sensing
rationale: Field microtremor surveys with DAS and nodal seismometers produce a shear velocity model, compared with seismic reflection. BOTDR and DTS monitor ground strain and temperature. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Adjoint Q tomography with central-frequency measurements in viscoelastic medium
rationale: Adjoint-state full-waveform Q tomography is physics-based inversion with no machine learning. The final 3D example uses a simulated DAS/VSP survey, so DAS counts as used, and all data are synthetic.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing of ocean-bottom seismo-acoustics and distant storms: A case study from Svalbard, Norway
rationale: The study records field DAS data on a submarine telecom cable in Svalbard, covering seismo-acoustic signals, sediment resonances and ocean swell. No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis relies on conventional signal interpretation.

title: Source parameter analysis using distributed acoustic sensing – an example with the PoroTomo array
rationale: Empirical Green's function spectral deconvolution is applied to observed PoroTomo DAS strain rate and nodal seismometer records; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS field data are analyzed directly.

title: Distributed Discharge Detection Based on Improved COTDR Method With Dual Frequency Pulses
rationale: An improved COTDR-based DAS system measured lab vibration and spark-discharge acoustic signals, so DAS data were analyzed. The discharge extraction algorithm is signal processing, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Near-Surface 2D Imaging via FWI of DAS Data: An Examination on the Impacts of FWI Starting Model
other_family_note: borehole lithology logs used for evaluation
rationale: FWI is a physics-based inversion with no machine learning mentioned. Field DAS data from a well-characterized site are inverted, and the resulting images are evaluated against borehole lithology logs.

title: Imaging distributed acoustic sensing-to-geophone conversion data: A field application to CO2 sequestration data
rationale: The authors apply a deep-learning conversion of DAS records to geophone-equivalent data and compare it with a physics-based method. They use field VSP DAS and geophone data from a CO2 sequestration site.

title: Anti-noise UWFBG-array enhanced DAS system using double-pulse-based time-domain adaptive delay interference
rationale: The paper proposes a DAS interrogation technique using double-pulse delay interference and demonstrates it experimentally on UWFBG arrays, recovering acoustic and vibration signals. No machine learning is mentioned; the processing is optical and conventional signal processing.

title: Real-Time Fiber-Optics Solution Opens Door to the Wellbore Environment
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) in wellbores
rationale: Describes a real-time streaming and processing system for field DAS and DTS wellbore data at Johan Sverdrup; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS data are acquired and analyzed for wellbore applications.

title: Low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing shape factors for fracture front detection
rationale: Uses displacement discontinuity simulations and the zero strain-rate location method, with no machine learning mentioned. LF-DAS strain-rate data are simulated, and the method is then applied to two field cases (Montney, Austin Chalk).

title: Challenges and best practices in interpreting crosswell strain signals to monitor multicrew zipper-fracturing operations
rationale: The study analyzes field LF-DAS crosswell strain data from two fiber cables during zipper fracturing, using visualization and interpretation methods. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Acquisition and near-surface impacts on VSP mini-batch FWI and RTM imaging in desert environment
rationale: Deep learning serves as an optimization framework for FWI, so it is unclear whether any learned model is trained or applied. Simulated SEAM VSP data compare DAS along the well with a geophone array.

title: Using Dark Fiber and Distributed Acoustic Sensing to Characterize a Geothermal System in the Imperial Valley, Southern California
rationale: The authors analyze two days of passive DAS records from dark fiber, using ambient noise interferometry and surface-wave inversion for Vs structure. No machine learning is mentioned. Heat flow and gravity appear only as consistency checks.

title: Machine learning in microseismic monitoring

title: Assessing Geological Deformation Across Spatial and Temporal Scales Using Distributed Fiber Optic Sensing
other_family_note: Brillouin and Rayleigh frequency shift fiber strain sensing (quasi-static distributed strain)
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the paper is a conceptual framework for fiber sensing. Example field datasets at the Aramco facility include DAS and LF-DAS, alongside Brillouin and Rayleigh frequency-shift strain measurements.

title: Fiber‐Optic Observations of Internal Waves and Tides
other_family_note: Ocean-bottom DAS used as a fiber temperature sensor (thermal transients from internal waves and tides), plus a tidal pressure signal
