rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from seafloor power cables near Gibraltar and Gran Canaria to measure temperature and tidal signals. No machine learning is mentioned. The sensed quantity is mainly temperature, not an elastic field.

title: Quasi-Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on Orthogonal Codes and Empirical Mode Decomposition
rationale: Proposes and experimentally demonstrates a quasi-distributed acoustic sensing (phi-OTDR) system on a 99.4 km fiber with measured strain noise. EMD and orthogonal coding are signal processing, not machine learning.

title: Fiber-Optic Sensor Array for Distributed Underwater Ultrasound Sensing
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work is a fiber interrogation method. A quasi-distributed acoustic sensing FBG array was tested experimentally in an underwater pool tracking ultrasound pulses, which counts as DAS acoustic sensing.

title: DAS with telecommunication fibre-optic cable in urban areas can record storm-induced seismic noise
rationale: Four months of field DAS recordings from an urban telecom fibre are compared with weather-station rainfall and wind using linear correlation. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Evaluation of the Capabilities of Distributed Acoustic Sensing with a Helical Fiber for Cross-Well Seismic Survey
rationale: The abstract compares DAS (straight and helical fiber) with hydrophone recordings in a field cross-well seismic survey and applies travel-time tomography and stacking. No machine learning is mentioned, so the AI role is none and DAS use is yes.

title: Interpretable denoising of distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profile data using adaptive consistent prior net
Estimation of Temperature Profiles using Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing from In-Well Measurements
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) and wellhead/downhole temperature gauges; LF-DAS used here to sense thermal strain (temperature) rather than an elastic wavefield
rationale: The authors analyze field low-frequency DAS from wells against DTS and gauges, using a physics-based inversion for temperature profiles. No machine learning is mentioned. The DAS family is ambiguous because the sensed quantity is temperature.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing in geophysics — Introduction
rationale: Special-issue introduction summarizing DAS papers; ML is mentioned only as one topic of the compiled papers, not the authors' own analysis. DAS is central, but no data analysis of its own is stated.

title: A Global and Multiscale Denoising Method Based on Generative Adversarial Network for DAS VSP Data
rationale: Authors propose DuGAN, a GAN with U-net generator, for denoising, and test it on both synthetic and field DAS VSP seismic data.

title: Field Trial of Coexistence and Simultaneous Switching of Real-Time Fiber Sensing and Coherent 400 GbE in a Dense Urban Environment
other_family_note: fiber-optic telecom signal quality (coherent 400 GbE QoT, ARoF transmission)
rationale: Field trial on Manhattan metro fibers running real-time DAS alongside coherent 400 GbE; DAS data inform path switching. No machine learning is mentioned. Telecom transmission quality measurements are coded as other.

title: Multiple Event Recognition Scheme Using Variational Mode Decomposition-Based Hybrid Feature Extraction in Fiber Optic DAS System
rationale: Experimental DAS intrusion signals are decomposed with VMD into hybrid feature vectors for event recognition. The recognition rates imply a trained classifier, but none is named, so the ML family is uncertain.

title: Nodal and Broadband Seismometer Complement to the Imperial Valley Dark Fiber DAS Array
rationale: A data-descriptor paper on broadband and nodal seismometer deployment with no ML mentioned. The DAS array is context: the stations complement it, but the abstract describes only seismometer data, not DAS data analyzed.

title: Smart Fiber-Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing (sDAS) With Multitask Learning for Time-Efficient Ground Listening Applications
rationale: The authors build a multitask learning network that recognizes and localizes ground events from DAS spatial-temporal samples. It is evaluated in a field test, so observed DAS data are analyzed.

title: Study Reviews Eagle Ford Parent-Well Frac-Hit Analysis, Prediction, and Mitigation
other_family_note: Oil-well surface pressure and production (rate, water cut, yield) records
rationale: The workflow uses empirical analysis, mechanistic models and a multivariate analysis prediction model, with no machine learning named. DAS appears only in a list of uncommon diagnostics that can detect frac hits, not as data analyzed.

title: Acquiring and processing deep dual-well DAS walkaway VSP in an onshore desert environment
other_family_note: sonic well log (borehole acoustic logging) used for comparison
rationale: Field acquisition and processing of dual-well DAS walkaway VSP, with conventional first-break picking, traveltime inversion, and migration. No machine learning is mentioned. Geophone VSP, surface seismic, and a sonic log serve as comparisons.

title: Earthquake location based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) as a seismic array
From strain to displacement: using deformation to enhance distributed acoustic sensing applications
rationale: The abstract describes a physics-based conversion of DAS strain to displacement, checked with full-waveform simulations and a real DAS dataset against collocated seismometers. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Borehole fibre-optic seismology inside the Northeast Greenland Ice Stream
rationale: Borehole DAS field experiment in Greenland ice recording active-source P and S waves; analysis uses traveltime tomography, surface waves and reverse-time migration, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Integrated Fading Suppression for Phase-Sensitive OTDR: An Algorithm Set
rationale: Abstract proposes combined conventional signal-processing denoising methods for fading in phase-sensitive OTDR DAS; no machine learning is mentioned. The methods are tested on 30 experimental DAS datasets, with strain noise reported.

title: Wavefield Modeling and Analysis of Lightning Quakes Measured by a Distributed Acoustic Sensing Array
rationale: No machine learning; the study uses 3D numerical simulations plus a data-driven strain-rate analysis. Lightning quakes were measured by a DAS array and analyzed, with phase velocities estimated from the DAS observations.

title: Annuli Liquid-Level Surveillance Using Distributed Fiber-Optic Sensing Data
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) in wells; DAS signal here largely reflects thermal effects at the fiber.
rationale: DTS and/or DAS field data from six well examples are used to track annulus liquid levels, with physical theory and simple models. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Spatial Deep Deconvolution U-Net for Traffic Analyses With Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Authors train a self-supervised U-Net to denoise and deconvolve car-induced DAS strain signals, evaluated on field DAS recordings of traffic; DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Real-Data Testing of Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Offshore Earthquake Early Warning
rationale: Uses real submarine DAS strain-rate recordings with arrival-time location and a magnitude scaling relation. It compares against onshore seismic stations and includes simulations. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Observations of Ocean Surface Wave Attenuation in Sea Ice Using Seafloor Cables
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS strain-rate data from a seafloor telecom cable on the Beaufort Shelf and calibrate it against wave buoy measurements. No machine-learning method is mentioned; the approach is a physical calibration.

title: Multiscale Encoder–Decoder Network for DAS Data Simultaneous Denoising and Reconstruction
rationale: Authors propose a multi-scale encoder-decoder CNN for joint DAS denoising and trace reconstruction, tested on synthetic and field DAS seismic data, so the AI is their method and DAS data were analyzed.

title: High resolution seafloor thermometry for internal wave and upwelling monitoring using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
other_family_note: DAS used as fiber-optic temperature anomaly sensing (non-elastic quantity); alternative optical fiber sensing technology for validation
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from a seafloor telecom cable as temperature sensors and validate against in-situ ocean sensors. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: An upper-crust lid over the Long Valley magma chamber
rationale: The authors image the caldera's subsurface using DAS recordings from a 100-km fiber cable. The abstract mentions no machine learning or AI method, so the analysis is conventional imaging of observed field data.

title: Inversion method for soil moisture content based on a distributed fiber optic acoustic sensing system
rationale: The authors use DAS field measurements of active-source seismic velocity to invert soil moisture, with validation against a water cut meter. Only a physical approximation and inversion are described; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: A Phase-Sensitive Optical Time Domain Reflectometry with Non-Uniform Frequency Multiplexed NLFM Pulse
rationale: The paper presents a phase-sensitive OTDR distributed acoustic sensing system, validated experimentally on a 16.3 km fiber with vibration response measurements. No machine learning is mentioned; the signal processing is conventional pulse compression and multiplexing.

title: An Object Storage for Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The paper presents cloud object storage and data formats for DAS, benchmarked on seismology use cases. It processes a month of observed DAS data with ambient noise cross-correlation. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Seismicity and seismic monitoring of Canada’s volcanic zones
rationale: Review of seismic monitoring history and seismicity catalogs at Canadian volcanic zones; no machine learning mentioned. DAS appears only as a new development in monitoring, not as data the authors analyzed.

title: Diffusion Model for DAS-VSP Data Denoising
rationale: Authors train a diffusion network (generative deep learning) on synthetic DAS-VSP data and apply it to denoise both synthetic and field DAS-VSP recordings, so DAS data are analyzed and observed data are included.

title: Ultra-high extinction ratio optical pulse generation with a thin film lithium niobate modulator for distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: A photonics hardware paper with no machine learning mentioned. The modulated pulses probe an experimental DAS system on a 2-km sensing fiber, and its strain sensitivity and crosstalk are measured, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: A High-Performance DAS System Using Point-Backscattering-Enhanced Fiber and Study of Its Noise Characteristics
rationale: Experimental and theoretical study of DAS system noise with enhanced backscattering fiber; DAS strain noise measured experimentally and simulated. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Fracture Conductivity Work Flow Models Well Spacing, Completions Design
other_family_note: laboratory proppant fracture-conductivity tests; well production history; unspecified field fracture diagnostics
rationale: Physics-based geomechanical and reservoir simulation with history matching, no machine learning. DAS appears in the HFTS-2 project overview. The models were calibrated with diagnostics, but the abstract does not say whether DAS data were among them.

title: LONG-PERIOD PRESSURE FLUCTUATIONS RECORDED BY FIBER-OPTIC SENSING TECHNOLOGY
rationale: Continuous DAS observations on a 120 km Muroto submarine cable are compared with nearby seafloor pressure gauge records during typhoons. Observed data only; no machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Integration of distributed acoustic sensing for real-time seismic monitoring of a geothermal field
rationale: The authors analyze six months of field DAS recordings from a borehole fiber at a geothermal site, plus a seismometer comparison. Denoising and event detection are described without any machine-learning method, so ai_role is none.

title: Experimental Study on Sand Detection and Monitoring Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Multiphase Flow in Horizontal Pipes
rationale: DAS data acquired on an experimental flow loop and analyzed with spectra, spectrograms and frequency band energy; no machine learning mentioned. Acoustic sensing of pipe flow counts as seismic_elastic; laboratory data are observed.

title: Technology Focus: Hydraulic Fracturing Modeling (November 2023)
rationale: Editorial technology-focus piece with no analysis of its own; DAS and data-driven modeling appear only as titles of recommended reading, not as methods or data used by this paper.

title: Detection of a CO2 plume by time-lapse analysis of Rayleigh-wave amplitudes extracted from downhole DAS recordings of ocean microseisms
rationale: Field downhole DAS recordings of ocean microseism Rayleigh waves analyzed over time during CO2 injection, plus theory and numerical simulation; no machine learning mentioned.

title: Optimization of hydraulic fracture monitoring approach: A perspective on integrated fiber optics and sonic tools
Large scale indoor occupant tracking using distributed acoustic sensing and machine learning
Surface distributed acoustic sensing for high-resolution near-surface characterization: Results from a 3D onshore field experiment
rationale: Field surface DAS data were processed with surface-wave inversion and compared to geophones, nodes and electrical resistivity tomography. No machine learning is mentioned, and DAS field data are analyzed directly.

title: Array analysis of seismo-volcanic activity with distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors analyse field DAS strain-rate records at Stromboli alongside nodal seismometers, using time-delay inversion and array analysis. No machine learning is mentioned anywhere in the abstract.

title: Research on the intrinsic phase difference of Rayleigh scattering in distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The study analyzes how a DAS phase-demodulation algorithm (3x3 coupler DCM) responds to pulse width, using both experimental and simulated DAS data. The abstract mentions no machine learning.

title: Fading Discrimination and Suppression of DAS System Based on FAM-MAE
rationale: Masked autoencoders reconstruct faded DAS signal positions, with DBSCAN clustering locating fading points. Experiments on Φ-OTDR DAS data from PZT vibration and underwater acoustic disturbances, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Prediction of fiber Rayleigh scattering responses based on deep learning
Protecting the weak signals in distributed acoustic sensing data processing using local orthogonalization: The FORGE data example
rationale: The denoising chain uses conventional filters (band-pass, median, f-k dip, curvelet) plus local orthogonalization, with no machine learning. It is applied to observed DAS recordings from the FORGE geothermal field.

title: An advanced median filter for improving the signal-to-noise ratio of seismological datasets
Development of a subsea distributed acoustic sensing acquisition system
rationale: The abstract describes a subsea DAS acquisition system and field zero-offset DAS VSP data acquired on two deepwater fields. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: On-chip silicon electro-optical modulator with ultra-high extinction ratio for fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Photonic hardware paper with no machine learning mentioned. The fabricated on-chip modulator is applied in a working DAS system, with measured strain sensitivity and crosstalk noise, so DAS data were used.

title: Full-waveform simulation of DAS records, response and cable-ground coupling
rationale: Particle-based numerical modelling of a virtual DAS cable and its ground coupling. No machine learning is mentioned. The analysis uses simulated DAS strain data only, with no observed records named.

title: Time-lapse attenuation variations using distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profile data during CO2 injection at CaMI Field Research Station, Alberta, Canada
rationale: The abstract describes a spectral attenuation (Q) measurement method with no machine learning. It applies the method to field time-lapse DAS VSP surveys from the CaMI CO2 injection site, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Real options of distributed DAS sensing applied to road transport engineering
rationale: Cost-benefit and real-options analysis of DAS for road transport; no machine learning mentioned. DAS is the central topic, but the abstract does not say whether any DAS measurements were analyzed. Cost and infrastructure records are inferred.

title: The Global DAS Month of February 2023
rationale: Dataset paper describing a coordinated global campaign of 32 DAS systems recording earthquakes; field DAS data were collected and shared. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Application of pipeline leakage detection based on distributed optical fiber acoustic sensor system and convolutional neural network
rationale: An RBF neural network classifies leakage signals and is compared with CNN, backpropagation and random forest. Experiments use distributed optical fiber acoustic sensing (DAS) to detect acoustic leakage signals from an underwater gas pipeline.

title: A Novel Three-Component Fiber-Optic Geophone for Distributed Acoustic Sensing System
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work is a hardware design with motion-equation derivation. A DAS-based three-component prototype recorded active-source vibration experiments and was compared with conventional geophones, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Detecting fractures and monitoring hydraulic fracturing processes at the first EGS Collab testbed using borehole DAS ambient noise
other_family_note: borehole core photos and core logs (geological core observations)
rationale: Field borehole DAS ambient noise analyzed by computing per-channel RMS amplitude profiles and comparing them with core photos and logs. No machine learning is mentioned; the processing is conventional signal analysis.

title: Long-term monitoring and analysis of Brood X cicada activity by distributed fiber optic sensing technology
rationale: The authors used DAS on telecom fiber cables in the field to record and analyze cicada acoustic signatures. The abstract mentions no machine learning or AI method.

title: News in Astronomy & Geophysics – December 2023
rationale: A news digest of astronomy items, awards and outreach events. It reports no original analysis by the authors, mentions no machine learning, and never mentions distributed acoustic sensing.

title: Signal propagation from portable active seismic source (PASS) to km‐scale borehole DAS for continuous monitoring of CO2 storage site
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning; it relies on signal stacking. Field signals from an active source were recorded on a borehole fiber DAS cable down to about 1 km depth.

title: Equivalent Near-Field Corner Frequency Analysis of 3D Dynamic Rupture Simulations Reveals Dynamic Source Effects
rationale: Physics-based dynamic rupture simulations and spectral corner-frequency analysis, with no machine learning mentioned. The synthetic waveforms are validated against observed near-fault spectra. DAS is named only as future potential data.

title: Oil-Water Flowing Experiments and Water-Cut Range Classification Approach Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Laboratory and field DAS acoustic recordings from oil wells were classified by water-cut range using a BP neural network, a decision tree and a random forest, so DAS data are analyzed directly with ML.

title: Seismic arrival-time picking on distributed acoustic sensing data using semi-supervised learning
rationale: Authors train PhaseNet-DAS, a deep network, on DAS records, using labels from pretrained PhaseNet refined by Gaussian mixture association. DAS earthquake data are analyzed directly; observed data implied by earthquake detection application.

title: Stochastic inversion for equivalent hydraulic fracture characterization using low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing data
Overhead Transmission Line Sag Monitoring Using a Chirped-Pulse Phase-Sensitive OTDR
rationale: CP-ΦOTDR distributed acoustic sensing measures wind-induced vibration strain on a power-line fiber. Sag is derived from the fundamental frequency through spectral analysis, with no machine learning mentioned. Observed field data are implied.

title: A review of distributed acoustic sensing applications for railroad condition monitoring
An Update on the Geothermal Data Repository's Data Standards and Pipelines: Geospatial Data and Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data: Preprint
other_family_note: drilling data and generic geospatial datasets handled by data pipelines
rationale: The paper describes data standards and pipelines meant to support geothermal machine learning, with no model applied. DAS is a central data type handled by the pipelines, but whether any DAS data were actually analyzed is not stated.

title: DAS-N2N: machine learning distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) signal denoising without clean data
rationale: Authors train a weakly supervised deep learning denoiser on field DAS recordings from the Rutford Ice Stream, Antarctica, enhancing icequake SNR. That supports AI as method and DAS used, with observed data.

title: Blast-Assisted Subsurface Characterisation Using a Novel Distributed Acoustic Sensing Setup Based on Geometric Phases
rationale: A novel DAS setup records strain from blast-generated surface waves on a field dark fiber. Dispersion analysis uses seismic interferometry, and shear-velocity inversion uses an evolutionary optimisation algorithm, which is optimisation rather than machine learning.

title: The Performance of Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Tracking the Movement of Road Vehicles
rationale: The abstract reports field experiments with DAS cables tracking road vehicles and measuring signal quality versus speed, size and installation. Processing is conventional signal handling; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Interpretation of low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing data based on geomechanical models
other_family_note: hydraulic fracturing pumping curves (treatment pressure/rate records)
rationale: The authors interpret observed low-frequency DAS strain waterfall plots alongside pumping curves, using a simple geomechanical model. No machine learning is mentioned, and DAS data are directly analyzed.

title: Few-Shot Classification with Meta-Learning for Urban Infrastructure Monitoring Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Authors train a meta-learning neural embedding network for few-shot event classification on preprocessed DAS data for urban infrastructure monitoring. The data source is not stated as field or synthetic, so simulated_only is null.

title: Eavesdropping on wastewater pollution: Detecting discharge events from river outfalls via fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing
CODAS Data from Oliktok Point, Beaufort Sea, Alaska
rationale: Dataset release of field DAS strain-rate recordings from dark telecom fiber in the Beaufort Sea; no machine learning is mentioned. The DAS data are observed, not simulated.

title: 3D near-surface P-wave velocity structure imaging with Distributed Acoustic Sensing and electric hammer source
rationale: Field active-source DAS experiment with seismometer comparison; STA/LTA picking and TomoDD travel-time inversion are conventional methods, no machine learning mentioned. DAS data were analyzed directly.

title: An Update on the Geothermal Data Repository's Data Standards and Pipelines: Geospatial Data and Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
other_family_note: drilling data; unspecified geospatial datasets
rationale: The paper describes repository data standards and automated pipelines meant to support geothermal machine learning, with no model applied. It implemented a DAS data pipeline, but whether this counts as analyzing DAS data is debatable.

title: Utah FORGE: Neubrex Well 16B(78)-32 Circulation Test Fiber Optics Monitoring Data and Reports - July, 2023
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) by fiber
rationale: Dataset release of field DAS strain, strain-rate and FBE data plus DTS from a FORGE circulation test; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data are the dataset content, so it counts as used.

title: Experimental research on signal sensing of distributed acoustic sensing optical fiber based on Φ-OTDR in shallow water
rationale: Shallow-water field experiments record underwater acoustic sources and a passing vessel with a Φ-OTDR DAS fiber. The analysis uses conventional processing such as time-delay differences; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Fiber-Optics Approach Monitors Drainage Profile of Multistage Stimulation
other_family_note: Reservoir pressure gauges in observation well; strain measured by Rayleigh frequency-shift distributed strain sensing (quasi-static fiber strain, treated as strainmeter-like)
rationale: Field case study correlating fiber-measured strain with pressure gauges; no machine learning mentioned. DAS appears only as a lower-resolution comparison; the data are Rayleigh frequency-shift strain sensing, not DAS.

title: Detection of microseismic events in continuous DAS data using convolutional neural networks
rationale: Authors develop and train a CNN to detect microseismic events in continuous field DAS recordings plus geophone arrival times from Utah FORGE; DAS is analyzed directly, and both DAS and geophones are seismic.

title: Real-time passive seismic monitoring using DAS — Today's solutions and remaining challenges
rationale: Authors describe their real-time DAS monitoring implementation, including deep learning-aided signal detection performed at the well site. DAS is central. Whether field data were analyzed is implied but not stated, so simulated_only is unclear.

title: Impact of Lossy Compression Errors on Passive Seismic Data Analyses
rationale: The study compares wavelet, zfp and SVD lossy compression, which are not ML methods. It applies them to two public field DAS datasets (urban dark fiber and a geothermal surface array), so DAS data were analyzed.

title: An Open-Access Data Set of Active-Source and Passive-Wavefield DAS and Nodal Seismometer Measurements at the Newberry Florida Site
rationale: Data set paper documenting field DAS and nodal seismometer recordings of active and passive seismic waves; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data were acquired, processed and released.

title: Exploiting the Potential of Urban DAS Grids: Ambient-Noise Subsurface Imaging Using Joint Rayleigh and Love Waves
rationale: Ambient-noise interferometry on urban DAS fiber in San Jose, with dispersion analysis and joint surface-wave inversion; no machine learning mentioned. Observed DAS data analyzed, supplemented by numerical experiments.

title: Using distributed acoustic sensing to characterize unconventional reservoirs via perforation-shot triggered P waves
other_family_note: well logs (borehole geophysical logging)
rationale: Field DAS recordings of perforation shots are analyzed for P-wave dispersion with signal processing and numerical modeling; no machine learning is mentioned. Results are compared with well logs and 3D seismic amplitude.

title: Silicon photonic integrated interrogator for fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The paper presents a silicon photonic chip interrogator for DAS and reports measured strain resolution on 12.1 km and 49.0 km sensing fibers. No machine learning is mentioned; DAS data are analyzed for performance evaluation.

title: Virtual Shear Checkshot from a Densely Sampled DAS Walkaway VSP in a Desert Environment
rationale: The study applies seismic interferometry, a conventional non-ML method, to field walkaway DAS VSP data and compares the result with a sonic log and geophone VSP. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Accurate Magnitude and Stress Drop Using the Spectral Ratios Method Applied to Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors apply empirical Green's function spectral ratios with Boatwright model fitting, with no machine learning involved. They analyze observed DAS recordings of earthquakes in Israel and compare them against an accelerometer network.

title: Can the seismic wave attenuation characteristics of various soils be identified using distributed acoustic sensing?
Overview of Health-Monitoring Technology for Long-Distance Transportation Pipeline and Progress in DAS Technology Application
rationale: A review of pipeline health-monitoring technologies with no machine learning mentioned. DAS is the central topic, but the abstract describes summarizing prior work, not analyzing DAS data of its own.

title: A Dual Attention Denoising Network for DAS VSP Signal Recovery and Its Interpretability Analysis
rationale: Authors propose and train a dual attention encoder-decoder denoising network on DAS VSP data. The semisynthetic dataset likely mixes real noise with synthetic signals, so whether all data are simulated is unclear.

title: Optimal Recovery of Rayleigh‐Wave Overtones by Multi‐Directional Acquisition
rationale: The work relies on eigenfunction theory, wave-equation modeling and statistical analysis, with no machine learning. The field examples explicitly include distributed acoustic sensing data, so DAS was analyzed alongside the simulations.

title: A semblance-based microseismic event detector for DAS data
rationale: Semblance-based coherence detector with thresholding and clustering criteria; no machine learning described. Applied to synthetic and real FORGE DAS microseismic recordings, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Machine Learning for Distributed Acoustic Sensing data (MLDAS) v1.0.1
rationale: Software package description for deep learning (PyTorch) on DAS data; no stated application of a model to specific data, so AI is the subject and whether DAS data were analyzed is unclear.

title: Low-Frequency Blast Detection Using a Large-N Dark Fiber in Noisy Environments: Template Matching and Optimal Channel Selection
rationale: Uses template matching, median absolute deviation and a voting scheme for channel selection, with no machine learning. Analyzes field DAS recordings of mining blasts on dark fiber in Imperial Valley and compares them with seismometers.

title: Quantitative Analysis of Hydraulic Fracturing Test Site 2 Completion Designs Using Crosswell Strain Measurement
rationale: The paper uses a Green-function displacement discontinuity inversion, which is physics-based, and no machine learning is mentioned. It analyzes field low-frequency DAS strain recorded in two HFTS-2 monitoring wells.

title: Efficient signal-to-noise ratio enhancement model for severely contaminated distributed acoustic sensing seismic data based on heterogeneous knowledge distillation
rationale: Authors build a ResNet20 teacher-student knowledge distillation network to denoise DAS seismic data; experiments apply it to DAS signals, though the abstract does not say whether the data are field or synthetic.

title: Coherently parallel fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing using dual Kerr soliton microcombs
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning. The authors build and demonstrate a dual-comb DAS system and report a measured strain detection limit, which implies experimental DAS data were analyzed.

title: Multi-Sensor Seismic Processing Approach Using Geophones and HWC DAS in the Monitoring of CO2 Storage at the Hellisheiði Geothermal Field in Iceland
rationale: Active-source field survey with helically wound cable DAS and geophones, processed via tomographic inversion and multichannel seismic processing; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data analyzed directly.

title: Remote condition monitoring of rail tracks using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS): A deep CNN-LSTM-SW based model
rationale: Authors train a CNN-LSTM with sliding windows on field DAS data from a 4.16 km fiber setup at a high tonnage load facility. The model classifies train position and normal versus abnormal rail conditions, so this is DAS vibration monitoring.

title: Imperial Valley Dark Fiber Project Continuous DAS Data
rationale: Dataset release of continuous field DAS recordings on dark telecom fiber in Imperial Valley for geothermal exploration; no machine learning mentioned, only file reading examples.

title: Potential of Earthquake Strong Motion Observation Utilizing a Linear Estimation Method for Phase Cycle Skipping in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS records along a Shinkansen railway fiber are analyzed with a linear estimation and RMS scaling to fix clipping, then compared with seismometer peak ground velocities; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Sensing Optical Fibers for Earthquake Source Characterization Using Raw DAS Records
rationale: Physics-based spectral strain modeling for source parameters; no machine learning mentioned. Real DAS surveys in Chile and Southern Apennines analyzed, compared with standard seismic instruments.

title: DAS sensitivity to heterogeneity scales much smaller than the minimum wavelength
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the study uses 2-D numerical modeling and homogenization theory. It analyzes simulated DAS strain-rate responses against velocity, so DAS is used with synthetic data only.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing-Based Weight Measurement Method
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; weight is recovered by inverting DAS phase changes. The authors ran indoor experiments using DAS fiber strain, so DAS data were analyzed. Strain sensing via DAS is coded as seismic_elastic.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing to Monitor Ground Motion/Movement at Multi-Frequency Bands
rationale: The paper proposes a DAS interrogation technique combining phase and spectral cross-correlation, validated experimentally. It uses no machine learning. DAS data were acquired in validation; ground-motion applications are stated only as potential uses.

title: Fully distributed fiber-optic streamer with small channel spacing for marine seismic acquisition
Detection of Earthquake Infragravity and Tsunami Waves With Underwater Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Uses frequency-wavenumber transforms, beamforming and a velocity correction on subsea DAS fiber data offshore Oregon; no machine learning is mentioned. The DAS strain records fall under seismic_elastic per the codebook.

title: Subsurface Imaging Using Interferometry of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Ambient Noise Measurement along a Dark Fiber Line: A Case Study in Downtown Reno, Nevada
rationale: The authors record DAS ambient noise on a 12 km dark-fiber line in Reno, then apply seismic interferometry and dispersion inversion for shear-wave velocity. A synthetic test is added. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Fiber-Optic Strain Measurements Aid Fracture Characterization
other_family_note: Rayleigh frequency shift distributed fiber-optic strain sensing (RFS-DSS) and downhole pressure gauges, simulated
rationale: A coupled geomechanics and fluid-flow simulator models fiber strain and pressure, with no machine learning mentioned. The fiber data are Rayleigh distributed strain sensing, not DAS; low-frequency DAS appears only as a comparison.

title: Toward a Metadata Standard for Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) Data Collection
rationale: The paper proposes a metadata schema for DAS experiments and mentions no machine learning. DAS is central, but the standard is only applied to deployment scenarios, so it is unclear whether any DAS time series were analyzed.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Crowd Motion and Firecracker Explosions in the Fireworks Show
rationale: Field DAS experiment during fireworks show analyzed with ambient noise cross-correlation, manual inspection and grid search; seismometers compared. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Monitoring volcanic activity with distributed acoustic sensing using the Tongan seafloor telecommunications cable
rationale: The authors recorded a week of DAS on a Tongan seafloor telecom cable, alongside onshore seismometers. They located earthquakes by picking P and S arrivals. No machine-learning method is mentioned.

title: Emerging technologies and advanced analyses for non-invasive near-surface site characterization
rationale: The abstract presents DAS and machine learning as emerging tools, then compares advanced applications at a case history. It never says whether ML or DAS data were actually applied in the authors' own analysis.

title: Analysis of DAS Seismic Noise Generation and Elimination Process Based on Mean-SDE Diffusion Model
rationale: Authors build a Mean-SDE diffusion model with a NAFnet noise predictor to denoise DAS VSP records. DAS seismic data are the analyzed target; the abstract does not say whether the experimental data are field or synthetic.

title: Monitoring ocean currents during the passage of Typhoon Muifa using optical-fiber distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from a submarine cable using frequency-wavenumber analysis and Doppler shifts, with no machine learning mentioned. They validate against sea-level and wind observations from a nearby buoy.

title: Monitoring underwater volcano degassing using fiber-optic sensing
rationale: A DAS cable was deployed in Laacher See and recorded acoustic bubble signals. Clustering algorithms, unspecified but implied unsupervised classical ML, grouped the events into four clusters. Field data, so not simulated.

title: Quality Control of DAS VSP Data in Desert Environment Using Simulations and Matching Filters
rationale: Field DAS VSP data are compared with finite-difference simulations and matching filters; no machine learning is mentioned. Geophone and checkshot data are also seismic, so DAS is used on observed data.

title: Measurement and Evaluation Method of Distributed Optical Fiber Acoustic Sensing Performance
rationale: Authors built a DAS test system and analyzed the resulting test data in the time-frequency domain. Evaluation uses the analytic hierarchy process, a decision method rather than machine learning, so no AI is applied.

title: Tracking Lightning Through 3D Thunder Source Location With Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Thunder events in urban fiber DAS data were picked manually and located by arrival times, with no machine learning. Results were compared against lightning detection and magnetic field data and weather radar reflectivity.

title: Characterize fracture geometry and propagation with low frequency distributed acoustic sensing strain data
The Impact of Quantization Bits on Coherent Detection DAS
rationale: The abstract derives a quantization-noise theory for coherent-detection DAS, validated by simulation and a 50 km field experiment. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Seismic observation using distributed acoustic sensing around the Tsugaru Strait at the Japan and Kuril Trenches, northeastern Japan
rationale: The authors recorded four months of offshore DAS data and located earthquakes by manually picking P and S arrivals. They derived an empirical magnitude relation and compared amplitudes with inland seismic stations. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Strain field reconstruction from helical-winding fiber distributed acoustic sensing and its application in anisotropic elastic reverse time migration
rationale: Physics-based strain reconstruction and reverse time migration; no machine learning mentioned. Helical-fiber DAS responses are analyzed, but only in two synthetic examples, so the DAS data are simulated.

title: Measuring hydrodynamics and exploring nearshore processes using distributed sensing of fiber-optic cable strain
rationale: Field DAS strain from a seafloor cable is compared with co-located pressure sensors through an empirical spectral transfer function and the cBathy algorithm. No machine learning is mentioned, so ai_role is none and das_used is yes.

title: GASF-ConvNeXt-TF Algorithm for Perimeter Security Disturbance Identification Based on Distributed Optical Fiber Sensing System
rationale: The authors train a ConvNeXt-tiny CNN with transfer learning on GASF-encoded φ-OTDR DAS signals recorded in field experiments on a 2.2 km cable. Transfer learning implies a pretrained model, so foundation_model is a tentative label.

title: A computerized system for Monitoring and informing about any unauthorized drilling operations near the cables.
rationale: A phase-OTDR DAS system on a buried fiber detects nearby drilling using wavelet denoising, high-pass filtering, autocorrelation and a threshold. No machine learning is used. It is unclear whether test activities at varied SNR were real or simulated.

title: Ice plate deformation and cracking revealed by an in situ-distributed acoustic sensing array
rationale: The authors applied an unspecified AI method to detect icequakes and low-frequency events in field DAS records from a frozen lake. Event activity was correlated with local temperature, which may be station air temperature.

title: A Surveillance System for Urban Utility Tunnel Subject to Third-Party Threats Based on Fiber-Optic DAS and FPN-BiLSTM Network
rationale: The authors train an FPN-BiLSTM deep network to classify third-party threat events. It is applied to fiber-optic DAS signals from field tests of an urban utility tunnel, which counts as DAS vibration sensing.

title: The role of artificial intelligence and IoT in prediction of earthquakes: Review
rationale: This is a review of AI and IoT approaches to earthquake prediction, with no original model applied to data. DAS, GPS, InSAR and seismometers appear only as background on past work, not as data the authors analyzed.

title: Fiber Seismic Network on the Moon
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the method is array stacking of seismograms. The authors compute synthetic lunar seismograms and evaluate DAS array configurations on them, so DAS is used with simulated data only.

title: UWFBG array vibration sensing technology for gas pipeline leakage detection and location
DAS Vehicle Signal Extraction Using Machine Learning in Urban Traffic Monitoring
rationale: The authors classify vehicle signals in field DAS recordings from Hangzhou using SVM, with random forest used for feature selection. DAS vibration data for traffic monitoring falls under the seismic_elastic family.

title: Detection of Large Dynamic Range Acoustic Signal Using OPD-Based Fiber-Optic Interferometric Demodulation With SNR Enhancement
rationale: Optical path difference demodulation of a Michelson fiber interferometer, tested by simulation and experiment; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS appears only as a possible future extension, so das_used is no.

title: Thousand‐Kilometer DAS Array Reveals an Uncatalogued Magnitude‐5 Dynamically Triggered Event After the 2023 Turkey Earthquake
rationale: The event was discovered in roughly 1,100 km of field DAS recordings and validated with local seismometers. The abstract mentions no machine learning; the analysis is conventional seismic detection and location.

title: Estimation of rock physics properties via full waveform inversion of vertical seismic profile data recorded by accelerometer and fibre-optic sensors
other_family_note: borehole well logs used to validate the inverted elastic models
rationale: The method is elastic FWI followed by Bayesian rock physics inversion with a Gaussian mixture prior, with no machine learning applied. Field VSP data from accelerometers and collocated DAS fibre are inverted and checked against well logs.

title: MFCC based real-time speech reproduction and recognition using distributed acoustic sensing technology
Embracing Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Car Cabin for Children Presence Detection
other_family_note: Airborne acoustic sensing with car-cabin speakers and microphones (not fiber-optic DAS)
rationale: No machine learning is named; detection relies on multipath acoustic signal design. The 'distributed acoustic sensing' here uses cabin speakers and microphones, not fiber-optic DAS, so das_used is no. Tests ran in real car cabins.

title: Ocean Bottom Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Oceanic Seismicity Detection and Seismic Ocean Thermometry
rationale: Uses ocean bottom DAS field data offshore Oregon, compared with OBS, for T-wave detection and thermometry. Curvelet denoising is a conventional transform method; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Microseismic Event Location with Dual Vertical DAS Arrays: Insights from the FORGE 2022 Stimulation
rationale: Uses a source-scanning algorithm and probabilistic uncertainty analysis, with no machine learning. Applied to field microseismic records from two vertical DAS boreholes at FORGE, plus synthetic geometry tests.

title: Partial Discharge Measurement for Power Cable Using Crosstalk-Free FDM-DAS
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work develops a frequency-multiplexed DAS system and applies it in laboratory discharge experiments on a power cable, detecting acoustic signals from partial discharges.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing microseismic reflection imaging for hydraulic fracture and fault lineament characterization
rationale: Uses Kirchhoff migration and wavefield separation on field downhole DAS microseismic data from Eagle Ford; low-frequency DAS strain also used. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Slickline-Deployed Fiber-Optic Cable Provides First Production Profile for High-Temperature Gas Well
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) by fiber; production logging spinner/pressure/temperature
rationale: Field case study analyzing DAS acoustic data and DTS thermal inversion in a North Sea gas well; no machine learning mentioned, only physics-based thermal inversion modeling.

title: 2D-SenseNet: A Simultaneous Demodulation and Denoising Network for DAS
rationale: Authors train a supervised deep network for joint demodulation and denoising of Φ-OTDR DAS signals on simulated data, then test it in a campus dark-fiber field experiment, so observed DAS data are analyzed.

title: Railroad condition monitoring with distributed acoustic sensing: an investigation of deep learning methods for condition detection
rationale: Authors train LSTM and GRU models on recorded railroad DAS signals to detect train presence, reporting detection rates; DAS vibration sensing of infrastructure counts as seismic_elastic with observed field data.

title: Fracture Height Quantification from Vertical and Horizontal Section Fiber Measurements: A Comprehensive Study Using LF-DAS Measurements from HFTS-2 Data Set
rationale: The study analyzes field low-frequency DAS strain data from HFTS-2 to estimate fracture height, using extension-compression transitions and a geomechanical inversion. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing for seismic surface wave data acquisition in an intertidal environment
other_family_note: borehole and seismic cone penetration test (SCPT) geotechnical data; hydrophones (ocean acoustics) also used
rationale: Field DAS surface-wave data from seabed fiber are compared against geophones, hydrophones, and borehole/SCPT data, then inverted for VS. No machine learning appears anywhere in the abstract.

title: Retrieval and precise phase-velocity estimation of Rayleigh waves by the spatial autocorrelation method between distributed acoustic sensing and seismometer data
rationale: Analytical SPAC/cross-correlation method with no machine learning mentioned; applied to actual seafloor DAS and vertical seismometer recordings, so DAS data were analyzed and data are observed.

title: Detecting wire breaks in prestressed concrete pipes: an easy-to-install distributed fibre acoustic sensing approach
rationale: DAS fibre system recorded acoustic signals from physically induced wire breaks on an experimental pipeline; analysis uses signal parameters (zero-crossing rate, short-time energy, duration) with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Reliable Earthquake Source Parameters Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data Derived from Coda Envelopes
rationale: The authors calibrate coda envelopes from field DAS data at Brady Hot Springs and an ESnet dark fiber, checking them against geophone and broadband records. No machine learning is mentioned; the processing is conventional coda calibration.

title: SigRecover: Recovering Signal from Noise in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data Processing
rationale: The authors apply a dictionary-learning framework, an unsupervised learned representation, to recover signal leaked into removed noise in DAS data. It is demonstrated on three DAS examples from the literature; whether those are field or synthetic is not stated.

title: DAS for 2-D MASW imaging: a case study on the benefits of flexible subarray processing
rationale: Field DAS active-source waveforms are reorganized into MASW subarrays to derive shear-wave velocity cross-sections, compared with invasive ground truth. No machine learning is mentioned; the processing is conventional surface-wave analysis.

title: Trial of shallow monitoring using DAS passive recordings
rationale: Field DAS passive ambient-noise surface-wave records and geophone data are analyzed for phase velocity estimation alongside modeling; no machine learning is mentioned, only conventional phase velocity methods.

title: Characterizing shallow fault zones by integrating profile, borehole and array measurements of seismic data and distributed acoustic sensing
other_family_note: borehole logging: core recovery and lithology changes
rationale: The abstract describes VSP tomography using geophones, borehole DAS behind casing and surface arrays, with no machine learning. The fault zone is supported by electrical conductivity logs and core/lithology logs.

title: Distributed Partial Discharge Acoustic Signal Detection and Localization Technology for GIL With Built-in Fiber Optics
rationale: DAS (coherent OTDR) sensing of partial discharge acoustic signals on a physical GIL test platform; acoustic field counts as seismic_elastic. No machine learning is mentioned; detection and localization are via the sensing system itself.

title: HD-TMA: A New Fast Template Matching Algorithm Implementation for Linear DAS Array Data and Its Optimization Strategies
rationale: The core method is template matching, which is non-ML. A neural network is proposed for building the template library, discussed on the Menyuan dataset, so its application is implied. Observed aftershock DAS data is compared with a seismometer.

title: Inference of Intermittent Hydraulic Fracture Tip Advancement Through Inversion of Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
Fiber-Optic Networks Could Reveal the Moon’s Inner Structure
rationale: Very short news-style abstract proposes lunar DAS networks as a possibility; no machine learning is mentioned, and no analyzed data are stated, so DAS is central but its use on data is unclear.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing in subsurface applications – Review and potential integration with artificial intelligence for an intelligent CO2 storage monitoring system
Temperature and Acoustic Field Reconstruction in Fiber Optic DAS System Based on Variational Mode Decomposition
other_family_note: fiber-optic temperature sensing (thermal strain measured from DAS Rayleigh phase)
rationale: Variational mode decomposition is a signal-decomposition method, not machine learning. Experimental phi-OTDR DAS measurements at high temperature separate acoustic signals from thermally induced strain, enabling dual-parameter temperature and acoustic sensing.

title: Assessing the feasibility of Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) for moonquake detection
Optimizing the Demodulation Method for DAS System Based on Point-Backscattering-Enhanced Fiber
rationale: The abstract describes theoretical noise analysis and averaging-based demodulation for a DAS system with enhanced fiber, and mentions no machine learning. Both simulations and experiments on DAS strain data are reported.

title: Urban subsurface exploration improved by denoising of virtual shot gathers from distributed acoustic sensing ambient noise
rationale: The analysis uses 15 days of field DAS recordings on dark fibre in Berlin. Methods are cross-correlation interferometry, coherence-based enhancement, and MASW inversion. No machine learning is mentioned, so ai_role is none.

title: Step-adaptive accelerated demodulation algorithm for LFM-pulse-based distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The paper presents an adaptive cross-correlation demodulation algorithm for LFM-pulse DAS, with no machine learning involved. Experimental results imply measured DAS data were processed, so DAS use is yes and the data are observed.

title: 3D DAS VSP for Coal Seam Exploration: A Case Study from Queensland, Australia
rationale: Field case study recording a 3D VSP with DAS fibre in boreholes for coal exploration; conventional seismic processing produced a 3D cube. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: 2-D Phase Unwrapping in DAS Based on Transport-of-Intensity-Equation: Principle, Algorithm and Field Test
rationale: The method is a physics-based, iterative TIE phase-unwrapping algorithm with no machine learning. Field DAS data are processed and compared against geophone recordings, and TDOA localization is applied to footstep signals.

title: Urban dark fiber distributed acoustic sensing for bridge monitoring
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from a Lyon telecom fiber to extract bridge modal frequencies, damping and mode shapes, checked against velocimeter data. No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis is conventional modal identification.

title: Near-surface characterization using shear-wave resonances: A case study from offshore Svalbard, Norway
rationale: Ocean-bottom DAS recordings of earthquake-triggered S-wave resonances on Svalbard telecom cables, plus active P-wave reflection data, are interpreted with physics-based estimation of layer thickness and velocity. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Using Vehicle‐Induced DAS Signals for Near‐Surface Characterization With High Spatiotemporal Resolution
rationale: The method relies on a Kalman filter, interferometry and surface-wave analysis, with no machine learning mentioned. It analyzes field DAS recordings from the Stanford DAS-2 array on telecom fiber.

title: Enabling endogenous distributed acoustic sensing in a digital subcarrier coherent transmission system
rationale: The paper describes an experimental DAS system that repurposes a communication training sequence for vibration sensing and reports measured strain sensitivity. Processing relies on a fractional Fourier transform; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Artificial intelligence-based distributed acoustic sensing enables automated identification of wire breaks in prestressed concrete cylinder pipe
Feasibility Study of Anisotropic Full-Waveform Inversion with DAS Data in a Vertical Seismic Profile Configuration at the Newell County Facility, Alberta, Canada
Seismic Magnitude Estimation Using Low-Frequency Strain Amplitudes Recorded by DAS Arrays at Far-Field Distances
rationale: Semiempirical spectral workflow with no machine learning mentioned. Field downhole DAS strain data from a hydraulic fracturing experiment, compared against surface geophone magnitudes, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Photonic Seismology: A New Decade of Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Geophysics from 2012 to 2023
Near real-time nautical depth mapping via horizontal optical fibers and distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors installed horizontal fibers and analysed continuous DAS recordings of passive acoustic sources to estimate water-mud interface depth. No machine learning is mentioned; the data are field observations.

title: The Improved Intrinsic Time-Scale Analysis for Multidimensional Signal-to-Noise Feature Separation of Borehole Seismic Data
rationale: Authors build a two-level ensemble of tree-structure learners to classify signal versus noise components in DAS VSP records; DAS data are the analyzed records, though whether field or synthetic is not stated.

title: Cosine Spectral Association Network for DAS VSP Data High-Precision Recovery
rationale: Authors propose a new deep learning network (CSANet) for denoising and recovering weak signals in DAS VSP data. Experiments are reported, but the abstract does not say whether the data were field or synthetic.

title: Monitoring of heavy loaded vehicles based on distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors train an EfficientNet CNN on Mel spectrograms of φ-OTDR DAS signals from a 47 km field fiber to classify vehicle load. Vehicle-induced vibration sensing with DAS counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Signal-and-Kernel Phase Noise Compensation Method for Distributed Acoustic Sensors
rationale: The paper proposes a signal-processing phase noise compensation method for Φ-OTDR DAS, demonstrated experimentally over 50 km of fiber measuring strain. No machine learning is mentioned; DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Locating clustered seismicity using Distance Geometry Solvers: applications for sparse and single-borehole DAS networks
rationale: The location method relies on distance geometry, least squares, rotational optimization and bootstrap, with no machine learning. It is applied to borehole DAS microseismic data at FORGE, plus Ridgecrest station recordings.

title: Illuminating Urban Near-Surface with Distributed Acoustic Sensing Multimodal Noise Surface-Wave Imaging
rationale: Observed DAS recordings from a repurposed telecom cable were processed with noise cross-correlation, frequency-Bessel transform, C3 interferometry, beamforming and dispersion inversion. No machine-learning method is mentioned.

title: 3D VSP Imaging Using DAS Recording of P- and S-Waves in Vertical and Lateral Well Sections in West Texas
rationale: The authors acquired and processed a field DAS VSP survey with vibroseis sources, using conventional VSP processing and first-break velocity analysis. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Seismic Monitoring of a Deep Geothermal Field in Munich (Germany) Using Borehole Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The abstract describes an automated detection, picking and source-characterization workflow on six months of field borehole DAS data, compared against seismometers. It names no machine-learning model, so ai_role is none; das_used is yes.

title: Improving Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data Quality With Self-Supervised Learning
rationale: Authors build a self-supervised dual-branch denoising network (blind spot based) and test it on field and synthetic DAS VSP seismic data, so DAS is used with observed data.

title: Deep Learning-Based Intrusion Detection and Impulsive Event Classification for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Across Telecom Networks
rationale: Authors train CNNs and vision transformers with multitask learning on DAS data from existing buried and aerial telecom cables for intrusion detection and acoustic event classification; camera integration is only mentioned as an add-on.

title: Whale detection and microseismic monitoring via DAS using submarine telecommunications cables – a case study from the NWS, Western Australia
rationale: Field DAS data from a 50 km subsea telecom cable were analyzed to detect whales, vessels and earthquakes. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Integrating distributed acoustic sensing and computer vision for real-time seismic location of landslides and rockfalls along linear infrastructure
Distributed shape detection for an acoustic sensitive optical cable with DAS
rationale: DAS signals from auxiliary acoustic sources are processed with a proposed adaptive peak allocation algorithm for 3D cable localization; no machine learning is mentioned. Demonstrated results with 6.53 cm error imply measured DAS data.

title: High‐density offshore seismic exploration with an optical fibre towed streamer based on distributed acoustic sensing: Concept and application
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; conventional processing workflow. Authors acquired and analyzed field DAS towed-streamer marine seismic data from a sea trial, so DAS is used on observed data.

title: Research on the processing and interpretation methods of distributed fiber optic vibration signal logging injection profiles
Modeling and simulation of Φ -OTDR system suitable for underwater intrusion detection and classification
Characterization of Gas–Liquid Two-Phase Slug Flow Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Horizontal Pipes
rationale: Laboratory DAS measurements of slug flow on a fiber wrapped around a pipe, processed with new non-ML algorithms and validated against high-speed camera video. No machine learning is mentioned, so ai_role is none.

title: SelfMixed: Self-supervised mixed noise attenuation for distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: Authors develop a self-supervised blind-spot deep prior network to denoise DAS data, tested on synthetic and field DAS records, so AI is the method and DAS data are analyzed.

title: Intelligent detection of loose fasteners in railway tracks using distributed acoustic sensing and machine learning
Fine-Amplitude Structure Localization Using Correlation Coefficients Between DAS VSP Data and Surface Seismic Data at the Same Interface
rationale: The method correlates DAS VSP data with surface seismic data using correlation coefficients, with no machine learning involved. DAS VSP data are analyzed directly. The abstract does not say whether the data are field or synthetic.

title: Quantitative multistage fracturing efficiency evaluation using cross-well strain measurements
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) in injection well
rationale: The method is a Green-function displacement discontinuity inversion with no machine learning. Field LF-DAS strain from a monitor well and in-well DAS plus DTS were analyzed for four treatment stages.

title: Single-shot multi-sensitivity distributed acoustic sensing with hardware envelope retrieving acceleration
rationale: A hardware DAS interrogation method using filtering and multi-bandwidth pulses; no machine learning is mentioned. The authors' own DAS measurements recover strain events and report processing times, implying observed experimental data.

title: Utah FORGE Project 3-2417: Simulations for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Strain Signatures as an Indicator of Fracture Connectivity
rationale: Dataset of physics simulations (COMSOL, discrete fracture network) producing synthetic DAS strain signatures; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data are simulated and analyzed, so das_used is yes and the data are simulated only.

title: High‐Frequency Tsunamis Excited Near Torishima Island, Japan, Observed by Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors analyze continuous ocean DAS records to detect tsunami signals and estimate source time series, then compare them with ocean-bottom pressure gauges. No machine learning is mentioned; the methods are conventional signal analysis.

title: Data Compression Solution for ϕ -OTDR: Encoding the Extracted Spectrum
rationale: AI is mentioned only as motivation; the method is spectrum-based data compression, with no ML applied. It compresses DAS Rayleigh backscatter signals, which implies analyzed DAS data, though whether the data are field or simulated is not stated.

title: Session 17. Oral Presentation for: Whale detection and microseismic monitoring via DAS using submarine telecommunications cables – a case study from the NWS, Western Australia
other_family_note: ocean acoustics (underwater sounds, whale vocalisations) sensed via DAS
rationale: Field DAS data from a 50 km subsea telecom cable were analyzed to detect whales, vessels and earthquakes. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned, so ai_role is none.

title: Deep learning model for fiber optic distributed acoustic sensing seismic data compression based on autoencoder and recurrent neural networks
rationale: Authors propose and evaluate a recurrent autoencoder (LSTM/RNN) for compressing DAS seismic data, reporting SNR results. DAS data are analyzed; the abstract does not state whether the data are field or synthetic.

title: Cold Diffusion Model for Seismic Denoising
rationale: Authors build and evaluate a cold diffusion deep learning model for denoising seismic waveforms. DAS is named only as a possible future application, so das_used is no. Data provenance (observed versus synthetic) is not stated.

title: Source Inversion Based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing-Type Data
rationale: Mathematical source inversion via an integral operator and constrained minimization, with no machine learning. DAS-type boundary data serve as the problem's data; numerical examples imply simulated DAS data only.

title: Experimental Investigation of Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensor Responses to Two Parallel Propagating Fractures
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; finite element modeling is physics simulation. A laboratory hydraulic fracture test used embedded distributed fiber strain sensors to emulate the low-frequency DAS strain response, so DAS-type data were analyzed.

title: Subspace projection attention network: Deep weak signal recovery from complicated downhole distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: Authors design and apply an attention-based neural network (SPANet) to denoise downhole DAS data, tested on synthetic and field DAS records, so DAS is used and data include observations.

title: Research note: Choosing gauge length for surface distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Abstract has no content beyond a data-sharing statement. The title centres on DAS gauge length choice, but whether DAS data were analysed cannot be told. No ML mentioned.

title: Tidally modulated seismic velocity changes observed using submarine dark fiber and the virtual-source method
rationale: The study applies ambient noise interferometry and virtual-source processing to MARS submarine dark-fiber DAS records, then compares velocity changes with tidal height data. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Application of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Technology in Pipeline Leakage Monitoring
rationale: Leak detection relies on FFT spectral analysis, energy attenuation and cross-correlation, with no machine learning. DAS fiber wound on a pipe senses leak vibrations in physical leakage experiments, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Assessing the Expansion of Ground-Motion Sensing Capability in Smart Cities via Internet Fiber-Optic Infrastructure
rationale: Geospatial coverage analysis using observed seismic noise and fiber/sensor infrastructure maps with an optimization; no ML. DAS motivates the study, but no DAS recordings appear to be analyzed, only potential fiber sensing coverage.

title: Application of machine learning for signal recognition in distributed fibre optic acoustic sensing technology
rationale: A review of feature extraction and pattern recognition for DAS, comparing traditional classifiers and deep learning; the authors analyze no data themselves. DAS is central, but no DAS data analysis is stated, so das_used is unclear.

title: Enhanced frequency and time domain feature extraction for communication infrastructure type classification using optical fiber sensing
rationale: Authors train a feedforward neural network on DAS signals from field optical cables to classify the surrounding infrastructure type (tunnel, duct, overhead), reporting 79-87% accuracy, so this is AI as method with DAS field data.

title: Subsurface Imaging by a Post-Stimulation Walkaway Vertical Seismic Profile Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing at the Utah FORGE Enhanced Geothermal System Site
rationale: Field walkaway VSP recorded with DAS at Utah FORGE, processed into depth images and interval Q using conventional seismic processing; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Mixed event separation and identification based on a convolutional neural network trained with the domain transfer method for a φ-OTDR sensing system
other_family_note: airborne audio recordings used for domain-transfer training
rationale: A CNN is trained on audio data, then fine-tuned and tested on φ-OTDR DAS data to separate and identify mixed events, so AI is the method and DAS data are analyzed.

title: Application of Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Geophysics Exploration: Comparative Review of Single-Mode and Multi-Mode Fiber Optic Cables
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing via multi-mode fiber, discussed in review
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. This is a literature review comparing single-mode and multi-mode fibers for DAS. DAS is central, but the abstract does not say whether the authors analyzed any DAS data themselves.

title: Detection of Track Bed Defects Based on Fibre Optic Sensor Signals and an Improved Hidden Markov Model
rationale: The authors train normal and abnormal hidden Markov models on features from DAS vibration signals of passing trains to classify track bed defects. This is learned statistical classification applied to field DAS data.

title: Characterization of low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing signals in hydraulic fracturing stimulation – A coupled flow-geomechanical simulation approach
rationale: A coupled flow-geomechanical fracture model in MRST simulates LF-DAS strain signatures, with no machine learning mentioned. Simulated DAS strain is compared qualitatively with field LF-DAS interpretations, so it is unclear whether observed data were analyzed.

title: Highway vehicle detection based on distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Random forest out-of-bag error is applied to select features of DAS road vibration signals. An experiment on highway vehicle detection implies observed DAS data were analyzed.

title: Ultrasonic measurements with embedded Fiber Bragg Gratings in polyurethane resins
other_family_note: Laboratory ultrasonic dynamic strain measured with embedded fiber Bragg gratings in polyurethane resin models (FBG spectra, curing/heat effects)
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. DAS appears only as motivation; the authors use point FBG sensors embedded in resin for lab ultrasonic strain tests, which fits laboratory physics rather than field seismic sensing.

title: Destructive Testing of the Pinkabach Railway Bridge – Large scale Testing of Sensor Systems for Fatigue Crack Monitoring and System Identification
other_family_note: Distributed fiber optic strain sensing (DFOS) on steel girders; Tiny Motion (likely camera-based displacement) for system identification
rationale: Bridge fatigue experiment testing DAS, acoustic emission, DFOS and Tiny Motion sensors with no machine learning mentioned. DAS was field-tested for structural system identification, so it is used.

title: Urban Dark Fiber Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Bridge Monitoring
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from telecom fiber in Lyon, checked against velocimeter data, to obtain bridge modal frequencies, damping and mode shapes. No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis is modal and structural dynamics.

title: Fading suppression and noise reduction of a DAS system integrated multi-core fiber
rationale: Experimental DAS system on 2.58-km multi-core fiber using spatial vector averaging for fading suppression; signal processing only, no machine learning mentioned. DAS data acquired and analyzed in the authors' own experiment.

title: A method for visualizing urban road events using distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The method relies on wavelet denoising, an RMS energy index and dynamic thresholding, with no machine learning mentioned. DAS data from urban telecom fiber were analyzed for vehicle, construction and subsurface cavity events.

title: Precision Traffic Monitoring: Leveraging Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Deep Neural Networks
rationale: Authors build a neural network framework to detect vehicles and estimate speed from DAS vibration data on telecom fiber, validated over multiple days against dedicated highway sensors. That supports deep learning as the method and observed DAS use.

title: Revealing complex subsurface dynamics with continuous seismic monitoring: Observations using distributed acoustic sensing and surface orbital vibrators during hydraulic fracturing
rationale: The authors analyze field time-lapse VSP data recorded by DAS with surface orbital vibrators, plus low-frequency DAS strain, during hydraulic fracturing. No machine learning method is mentioned.

title: Integrated Amphibious Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Seismic Monitoring in the Xinfengjiang Reservoir
rationale: Field DAS deployment across land and reservoir bottom, compared with shore seismometers for microseismic detection and noise analysis. No machine learning method is mentioned; analysis is conventional detection and SNR comparison.

title: Polarization sensing of network health and seismic activity over a live terrestrial fiber-optic cable
other_family_note: State-of-polarization sensing from telecom optical transceivers; telecom network health and traffic-loss records
rationale: Over 85 days, DAS measurements were collected on colocated cables as ground truth for polarization sensing. Network-health modeling is mentioned, but the abstract names no machine-learning method, so AI is none.

title: Geophysical Observations of the 2023 September 24 OSIRIS-REx Sample Return Capsule Reentry
other_family_note: infrasound (ground-based and balloon-borne atmospheric acoustic sensors)
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. The campaign deployed seismic, DAS, GPS and infrasound sensors, and the paper reports signal detections across these instruments, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Characterizing South Pole Firn Structure With Fiber Optic Sensing
other_family_note: firn core density measurements (SPICEcore)
rationale: The authors record DAS on an existing South Pole fiber and use geophones for ambient noise interferometry. Velocity inversion and empirical density relationships are conventional, with no machine learning mentioned. Ice core density data are also used.

title: SEED-Net: A High-Performance Phase Demodulation Network for DAS
rationale: Authors train an end-to-end demodulation neural network on synthetic DAS signals and test it on indoor and campus field DAS data, so AI is the method, DAS is used, and observed data are included.

title: Limits of Measurable Perturbation Rate in Time-Expanded Phase-Sensitive OTDR
rationale: Abstract analyzes dynamic range of a time-expanded phase-sensitive OTDR DAS system and experimentally demonstrates a new post-processing algorithm; no machine learning is mentioned. Strain/perturbation sensing with DAS is used experimentally.

title: Shallow Soil Response to a Buried Chemical Explosion With Geophones and Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field geophone and DAS recordings of a buried explosion are analyzed for resonance frequency shifts and the healing process; the abstract mentions no machine learning, only conventional spectral analysis.

title: Multidimensional information fusion and broad learning system-based condition recognition for energy pipeline safety
Depth calibration of distributed acoustic sensing data using well log ties
other_family_note: borehole well logs used to build the synthetic seismogram
rationale: DAS VSP data are depth-calibrated using dynamic time warping between a corridor stack and a well-log synthetic seismogram. DTW is a classical alignment algorithm, not machine learning, and DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Multiple noise reduction for distributed acoustic sensing data processing through densely connected residual convolutional networks
Submarine Cable-Based Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Tide Monitoring
rationale: A DAS interrogator recorded tide-induced vibration along a real submarine cable. Results are compared with tide-level variation, implying observed sea-level reference data. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: State-of-The-Art application and challenges of optical fibre distributed acoustic sensing in civil engineering
rationale: This is a review of DAS applications and challenges in civil engineering. It mentions no machine learning. DAS is central, but the abstract describes no data analyzed by the authors, so DAS use is unclear.

title: Phase unwrapping error identification and suppression method in φ-OTDR systems based on PELT-VMD-ARIMA
rationale: The method combines PELT changepoint detection, VMD and ARIMA, which are conventional signal-processing and statistical tools, not ML. It analyzes φ-OTDR (DAS) data from simulations, PZT lab experiments and an active-source seismic field test.

title: Advances in rock physics for pore pressure prediction: A comprehensive review and future directions
rationale: A review of rock physics for pore pressure prediction. It discusses machine learning as one reviewed advance but applies no model to data. DAS appears only as a future direction, and there is no original data analysis.

title: DAS Noise Suppression Network Based on Distributing-Local-Attention Expansion
rationale: Authors propose and test a CNN-transformer U-shaped network (Urefiner) for denoising DAS VSP records; experiments report noise suppression on DAS VSP data, though whether field or synthetic is not stated.

title: Previously hidden landslide processes revealed using distributed acoustic sensing with nanostrain-rate sensitivity
rationale: Field DAS low-frequency strain data from the Hollin Hill landslide were analyzed during rainfall to quantify strain-rate changes. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned; the analysis is direct strain observation.

title: DASPy: A Python Toolbox for DAS Seismology
rationale: Software toolbox using classic signal processing (filtering, denoising, spectral analysis); no machine learning mentioned. Demonstrates modules on openly available observed DAS data, so DAS is used.

title: Noise attenuation in distributed acoustic sensing data using a guided unsupervised deep learning network
rationale: Authors build an unsupervised deep learning denoiser with self-attention and apply it to field DAS recordings from SAFOD and FORGE fiber-optic cables, so DAS data are analyzed with a DL method.

title: DASCore: a Python Library for Distributed Fiber Optic Sensing
rationale: This describes a Python software library for DAS data processing, I/O and visualization, and mentions no machine learning. DAS is central, but the abstract states no specific dataset being analyzed, so DAS use is unclear.

title: Eigenfrequency analysis using fiber optic sensors and low-cost accelerometers for structural damage detection
Frequency‐Bessel Transform Method for Multimodal Dispersion Measurement of Surface Waves From Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: The paper extends an analytical frequency-Bessel transform, with no machine learning mentioned. It is tested on synthetic Green's functions and applied to three field DAS ambient-noise datasets, on land and seabed.

title: Evaluation of Fluid Distribution and Perforation Erosion in Multistage Fracture Treatment
