other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing (DTS) with reservoir thermal model
rationale: Physics-based interpretation models of field DAS frequency-band energy and DTS cooling, checked against downhole camera erosion images; no machine learning mentioned. DAS field data directly analyzed.

title: Offset VSP acquired with a single-use fiber-optic probe: Gorgon CCS case study
rationale: Field offset VSP recorded with bare fiber DAS in CO2 injection wells at Gorgon; analysis covers data quality, noise, and geometry effects. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Monitoring Water Level of a Surficial Aquifer Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Ballistic Surface Waves
rationale: Field DAS data from a trenched fiber in Fairbanks processed with MASW, surface wave inversion and a rock physics model. No machine learning is mentioned. Hydraulic head and precipitation records are compared against velocity changes.

title: DFOS Technology in Geoengineering Monitoring in the Past 35 Years: A Bibliometric Analysis
rationale: A bibliometric text-mining review of publications. Machine learning and DAS appear only as trending author keywords; no model or DAS data is analyzed. The data are Web of Science publication records, coded as human-system records.

title: Flow monitoring in a bubble column reactor by Distributed Acoustic Sensing
other_family_note: hydrophone acoustic measurements in a laboratory reactor
rationale: Experimental DAS monitoring of a bubble column reactor detects vibration patterns and is compared against a hydrophone. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS senses an elastic/acoustic field, so it codes as seismic_elastic.

title: Learnable dual attention fusion network for borehole distributed acoustic sensing systems data reconstruction
rationale: Authors propose and train a dual attention ResBlock network for denoising borehole DAS VSP data, tested on both simulated and actual records, so DAS data are analyzed and observed data are included.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing Signal Model Under Static Fiber Conditions
other_family_note: DAS interrogator Rayleigh backscatter (OTDR) signal under static fiber, with no external elastic or acoustic field sensed
rationale: A statistical, equation-based model of DAS backscatter amplitude and phase; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS signals are modeled and compared with experiments, but the Python-run experiments may be simulations, so whether data are observed is unclear.

title: DAS seismic signal recovery with non-uniform noise based on high-low level feature fusion model
Multigrid Spatially Constrained Dispersion Curve Inversion for Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS)
rationale: The method is a multigrid spatially constrained dispersion curve inversion, a conventional inversion with no machine learning mentioned. It is tested on synthetic data and applied to field DAS surface-wave data from Imperial Valley.

title: Hybrid CNN-LightGBM Architecture for Earthquake Event Classification in DAS Systems
Distributed strain sensing using Bi-metallic coated fiber optic sensors embedded in stainless steel
RDA-Net: A multi-cascade network for DAS background noise attenuation
Shallow Subsurface Imaging Using Challenging Urban DAS Data
rationale: Passive urban DAS data recorded on telecom fiber in Bern are processed with noise correlations and Rayleigh-wave dispersion inversion. The abstract mentions no machine learning method.

title: Multi-source wavefield reconstruction of distributed acoustic sensing data using compressive sensing and seismic interferometry
rationale: Uses compressive sensing with Fourier and curvelet sparsity plus seismic interferometry, with no machine learning. The analysis is applied to ambient DAS records from a fiber array in Perth, so the data are observed.

title: Enhancing subsurface seismic profiling with distributed acoustic sensing and optimization algorithms
other_family_note: borehole stratigraphic profiles used for validation
rationale: Field DAS ambient noise recordings were analyzed. An unsupervised clustering method selected data clusters before Green's function extraction, which counts as applied classical ML. The GA-MC inversion itself is optimization, not ML.

title: Passive Bidirectional Audio-Over-Fiber System Integrating Sensing, Power Supply, and Communication
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. The uplink uses DAS for distributed audio sensing over 10 km of fiber, with measured SNR and frequency response reported. That points to an experimental acoustic-field DAS demonstration.

title: Intrusion Event Classification of a Drainage Tunnel Based on Principal Component Analysis and Neural Networking
rationale: Authors trained an artificial neural network, compared against Bayesian and logistic regression classifiers, on PCA-reduced DAS signal features. The features come from a physical tunnel intrusion test system with rockfall and water release events.

title: DAS to discharge: using distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) to infer glacier runoff
rationale: Authors test several ML regression models on field DAS data from Rhonegletscher to predict stream-gauge discharge, and compare against models trained on meteorological station data. ML model types are not named.

title: Gas leakage physical simulation and its distributed optical fiber sensing experiments in the casing annulus of injection-production pipe column for underground gas storage
FiberFlex: Real-time FPGA-based Intelligent and Distributed Fiber Sensor System for Pedestrian Recognition
rationale: An in-house DAS system records ground vibrations from footsteps. Neural networks are trained on the labeled field data for pedestrian recognition and run on an FPGA, tested with real subjects.

title: EXPERIENCE OF USING FIBRE OPTIC DISTRIBUTED ACOUSTIC SENSING SYSTEMS IN VSP-OVSP SURVEY
rationale: Field VSP survey recorded wavefields with both DAS fibre and three-component geophones, then compared them; no machine learning or AI method is mentioned anywhere in the abstract.

title: Ambient noise imaging for municipal solid waste landfill structure detection based on the common-midpoint two-station analysis with distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS ambient noise processed by cross-correlation, dispersion measurement and gradient-based inversion; no machine learning is mentioned. The resulting velocity section was validated with high-density resistivity, which counts as electrical measurement.

title: Low-Frequency Vibration Detection Enhancement in Dual-Pulse DAS With Single AOM
rationale: Hardware phi-OTDR DAS scheme using dual-pulse probing with weighted averaging and reference subtraction; experimental vibration measurements on DAS. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Understanding Strain Signals from Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing In-Well Measurements: Experimental and Numerical Modeling
other_family_note: laboratory spring displacement tracking experiment (mechanical analog)
rationale: The authors compare field low-frequency DAS well strain data with a spring experiment and mass-spring models. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS field data are analyzed, so das_used is yes.

title: Multisource Threatening Event Recognition Scheme Targeting Drone Intrusion in the Fiber Optic DAS System
rationale: The authors apply a CNN+LSTM+self-attention model to recognize intrusion events in fiber-optic DAS signals. They report experimental accuracies on drone, wind and human-contact events, implying observed DAS data for perimeter security.

title: Evaluation of a Rapid Diagnostic Tool to Estimate Geometry Evolution of Multiple Simultaneously Propagating Fractures from Crosswell Fiber-Optic Strain Measurements
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; a physics-based zero strain rate location method is applied to simulated crosswell LF-DAS strain rate fields and then to a field multicluster case, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Feasibility Study and Results from a Baseline Multi-Tool Active Seismic Acquisition for CO2 Monitoring at the Hellisheiði Geothermal Field
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning; it describes seismic modeling, multichannel processing and quality control. The authors analyze field data from a helically wound DAS cable alongside geophones in an active seismic survey.

title: Reviews
rationale: Book reviews; one reviewed book concerns DAS, but the abstract describes no data analysis by the authors and mentions no machine learning. DAS is only the subject of a reviewed book.

title: Submarine Optical Fibers: A Window into Climate Change
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. DAS is the central topic, but this very short, perspective-like abstract does not say whether any DAS data were analyzed, so das_used is unclear.

title: Imaging of train noise with heavy traffic events recorded by distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS recordings of heavy train noise near Qinhuangdao processed with interferometry, spectral whitening, F-K stacking and dispersion inversion; no machine learning mentioned.

title: Advances in CO2 injection and monitoring technologies for improved safety and efficiency in CCS projects
rationale: Review of CCS injection and monitoring technologies; no ML mentioned beyond 'intelligent injection systems'. DAS, 4D seismic, satellite imaging listed only as reviewed technologies, with no own data analysis described.

title: Low-Altitude UAV Surveillance System via Highly Sensitive Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: A fiber DAS system records UAV-induced acoustic signals in a field test. Positioning relies on TDOA, generalized cross-correlation and least-squares estimation, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Multilayer Structure Damage Detection Using Optical Fiber Acoustic Sensing and Machine Learning
rationale: Laboratory DAS measurements of mechanical waves in a multilayer structure were classified for damage with a supervised SVM reaching 93% accuracy. Point sensors served as reference. DAS is the authors' own observed data.

title: Near Real‐Time In Situ Monitoring of Nearshore Ocean Currents Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on Submarine Fiber‐Optic Cable
rationale: A submarine DAS cable recorded ocean-wave signals, inverted via frequency-wavenumber dispersion analysis with no ML. Results were validated against a current meter and tide gauge (oceanographic in situ). Field DAS data were analyzed.

title: Detection and characterization of icequake swarms using distributed acoustic sensing in the Beaufort Sea
Pipeline leakage identification method based on DPR-net and distributed optical fiber acoustic sensing technology
DASEventNet: AI‐Based Microseismic Detection on Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data From the Utah FORGE Well 16A (78)‐32 Hydraulic Stimulation
rationale: Authors train and apply a ResNet convolutional network to detect microearthquakes in field DAS recordings from the Utah FORGE stimulation, compared against STA/LTA; observed data, DAS central.

title: High-spatial-resolution quasi-distributed acoustic sensing with phase noise suppression based on φ-OFDR
rationale: Abstract describes a quasi-distributed acoustic sensor based on phi-OFDR that demodulates experimental vibration signals, so DAS data are analyzed. Noise suppression uses optical hardware and a phase index method; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Design and Evaluation of Real-Time Data Storage and Signal Processing in a Long-Range Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) Using Cloud-Based Services
rationale: Cloud storage pipeline (DynamoDB) and CloudSim performance evaluation for DAS data handling; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data storage and processing is evaluated, though whether data are real or synthetic is not stated.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing technology in marine geosciences
rationale: This is a review summarizing DAS applications in marine geoscience, with no machine learning mentioned. DAS is the topic, but the abstract describes no analysis of the authors' own DAS data.

title: Ultrasonic Lamb wave detection using a fiber-optic quasi-distributed acoustic sensing system
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; empirical mode decomposition is conventional signal processing. A fiber-optic quasi-distributed acoustic sensing system recorded elastic Lamb waves on an aluminum plate in laboratory experiments, counted here as DAS.

title: Suppression of the interference fading in heterodyne Φ-OTDR with fast signal synthesis algorithm
rationale: Signal processing algorithm (time-domain stitching, complex moving average) for fading suppression in Φ-OTDR DAS; no machine learning. Experimental DAS results reported, so observed DAS data analyzed.

title: Coherent fading suppression of distributed acoustic sensing based on time–frequency domain linkage algorithm
rationale: The authors apply morphological component analysis to experimental DAS Rayleigh scattering data to suppress fading and compare it with mean and wavelet filters. No machine learning is used, which places the work in signal processing.

title: Codes for "Shallow Soil Response to a Buried Chemical Explosion with Geophones and Distributed Acoustic Sensing" DAG - 01101646
rationale: Code release reproducing figures from processed geophone and DAS recordings of a buried explosion during the Source Physics Experiment; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS field data were analyzed.

title: Assessing the Earthquake Recording Capability of an Ocean-Bottom Distributed Acoustic Sensing Array in the Sanriku Region, Japan
rationale: The authors analyze field ocean-bottom DAS records from Sanriku against a collocated OBS. Detection relies on waveform and spectrum similarity search, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Narrow linewidth III-V-on-SiN laser with extended frequency chirp capability based on micro-transfer printing for high resolution distributed acoustic sensing
other_family_note: Photonic laser characterization (linewidth, frequency chirp linearity) of a III-V-on-SiN source
rationale: A photonic laser device paper with no machine learning. The title targets distributed acoustic sensing, and the abstract reports a preliminary distributed fiber sensing measurement with the laser, implying DAS data were acquired.

title: Wavefield Reconstruction of Distributed Acoustic Sensing: Lossy Compression, Wavefield Separation, and Edge Computing
rationale: Authors test deep learning architectures (INR, SHRED recurrent decoder) on DAS data, reconstructing earthquake and ocean-wave wavefields for compression and separation; observed DAS fiber data are implied.

title: Multi-Frequency Φ-OTDR DAS Using Timely-Updated Vector-Based Phase Averaging
rationale: The paper proposes a dynamically updated vector-based phase averaging signal-processing method with no machine learning. It is demonstrated on laboratory and field DAS data, sensing vibrations from vehicles and wind on deployed telecom cables.

title: Investigation of the Reduction in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Signal Due to Perforation Erosion by Using CFD Acoustic Simulation and Lighthill’s Acoustic Power Law
rationale: The abstract describes CFD acoustic simulation and Lighthill's power law, with no machine learning mentioned. The simulated sound reduction is compared against observed DAS field data, so DAS is used and data are not purely synthetic.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing: A Promising Tool for Finger-Band Anomaly Detection
rationale: An experiment on monorail track vibration used DAS, with time- and frequency-domain signal analysis. No machine learning is mentioned. Observed DAS vibration data count as seismic_elastic.

title: Automatic Monitoring of Rock‐Slope Failures Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Semi‐Supervised Learning
rationale: Authors build a semi-supervised neural network and apply it to field DAS recordings of rock collapses in Brienz. Doppler radar data provide partial ground-truth labels, so radar counts as a second measurement family.

title: Transfer Learning-Based Seismic Phase Detection Algorithm for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Microseismic Data
rationale: The authors take the GPD neural network, pretrained on STEAD earthquake records, and fine-tune it via transfer learning on labeled borehole DAS microseismic data from Utah FORGE. Seismometer and DAS records are both observed seismic data.

title: A Preliminary Study on 2D Convolutional Neural Network‐Based Discontinuous Rail Position Classification for Detection on Rail Breaks Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: Authors train a 2D CNN on STFT spectrograms of DAS vibration data collected on an actual railway line to classify discontinuous rail positions; DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Sediment Corrections for Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The work uses physical first-order wave-propagation modeling and inversion, with no machine learning mentioned. It analyzes observed DAS recordings of earthquakes on a continental margin to calibrate sediment corrections for hypocenter localization.

title: From Labquakes to Megathrusts: Scaling Deep Learning Based Pickers Over 15 Orders of Magnitude
other_family_note: laboratory acoustic emission sensor recordings (lab rock physics)
rationale: Applies and augments pre-trained deep learning phase pickers from SeisBench, benchmarking on real data that explicitly include distributed acoustic sensing recordings, lab acoustic emission events, and tectonic earthquakes.

title: A Universal Denoiser for DAS-VSP Data Based on Semantic Mask and Random Mask Training
rationale: Authors propose and train a deep learning denoiser (masking scheme, segmentation subnetwork, attention mask) and test it on synthetic plus two field DAS-VSP datasets, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Assessing the value of combined use of distributed acoustic sensing and multicomponent vertical seismic profiling data with network-based full-waveform inversion and uncertainty quantification: A case study in Alberta, Canada
rationale: The authors run a recurrent-neural-network-based FWI on field Snowflake VSP baseline data that combine borehole DAS and accelerometer records. The RNN here is a physics-based FWI formulation, so its status as learned ML is somewhat uncertain.

title: High-resolution observations of shallow-water acoustic propagation with distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors analyze field DAS recordings from the MVCO telecom cable, using a two-step inversion for channel localization plus numerical simulations. No machine learning is mentioned. DAS data are observed, with simulations used for comparison.

title: Far-field radiation patterns of distributed acoustic sensing in anisotropic media with an explosive source and vertically straight fiber
rationale: Analytical derivation of DAS radiation patterns in anisotropic media; no machine learning mentioned. DAS strain-rate responses are derived and checked with synthetic examples only, so DAS is used via simulation.

title: Modelling uncertainty in P-wave arrival-times retrieved from DAS data: case-studies from 15 fibre optic cables
rationale: Applies a standard seismological picker and MCMC inversion, with no machine learning. Uses both synthetic and observed DAS arrival times from 15 fibre cables for locating seismic events.

title: Present status and prospective on the seismic hazard studies of major seismic gaps in the Sichuan-Yunnan region
Geophysical Monitoring Technologies for the Entire Life Cycle of CO2 Geological Sequestration
rationale: A review of CO2 storage monitoring methods (seismic, DAS/DTS fiber, neutron logging). No machine learning is mentioned. DAS is a central topic, but the abstract does not say the authors analyzed any DAS data.

title: Research on gas pipeline leakage identification based on SE-2DCNN with ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating distributed acoustic sensing system
rationale: Authors train an SE-attention 2D CNN on MFCC features of DAS acoustic data collected in a laboratory leak experiment. DAS senses acoustic leak signals, so the measurement is seismic_elastic and the data are observed.

title: Quasi-distributed acoustic sensing based on optical path difference demodulation for high-frequency and large-amplitude using an optical fiber interferometer array
rationale: The paper proposes an optical path difference demodulation scheme for quasi-distributed acoustic sensing with a UWFBG array. The scheme is validated experimentally on acoustic strain signals, so DAS data are analyzed. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Improved Cepstrum Analysis for Multiplicative Noise in Borehole Seismic Acquisition Records
rationale: Uses an enhanced cepstrum signal-processing method, no machine learning, applied to a real borehole DAS common-shot-point record to characterize multiplicative optical noise.

title: Utah FORGE: GES Well 16A(78)-32 and Well 16B(78)-32 Stimulation Seismic Event Catalogs
other_family_note: hydraulic injection/stimulation records (injection pressure/rates)
rationale: Dataset release of microseismic catalogs from geophones and DAS at Utah FORGE; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data were collected and used for event detection and location.

title: An adaptive parameter-free seismic data denoising approach by combining general cross-validation thresholding and pixel connectivity in synchrosqueezed domain
rationale: Denoising relies on signal processing (SS-CWT, GCV thresholding, pixel connectivity) with no machine learning. Tested on synthetic and real land, ocean, and DAS seismic records, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: A real scale application of a novel set of spatial and similarity features for detection and classification of natural seismic sources from distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: Authors apply XGBoost with custom spatiotemporal features to classify earthquakes and quarry blasts in field DAS recordings from a 91 km Pyrenees cable; catalogue events serve as reference.

title: Investigation on Sensor Layout of Optical Fiber Distributed Acoustic Sensing Technology for Flow Velocity Measurement in Pipes
rationale: The authors analyse DAS fiber phase changes on water-filled pipes, validated with FBG strain sensors, and relate them to flow velocity by quadratic fitting. No machine learning is mentioned; the fitting is conventional statistics.

title: Inclined bending seismic reflection layer in the crust illuminated by distributed fibre-optic-sensing measurements in western Japan
rationale: The study records local earthquakes on a 50 km DAS cable and interprets crustal reflections through numerical strain-rate simulation. No machine learning is mentioned. The observed field DAS data make das_used yes and simulated_only false.

title: Poroelastic Effects in Analysis of Pore Pressure and Strain Around a 3D Propagating Hydraulic Fracture
rationale: A physics-based 3D hydromechanical cohesive-zone model simulates pore pressure and strain, with no machine learning. DAS appears only as background on conventional monitoring interpretation, and the simulated strain is not described as DAS data.

title: Performance of synthetic DAS as a function of array geometry
rationale: The study uses forward-modelled synthetic DAS data, analysed with array response functions, beamforming and back-projection to compare array geometries. No machine-learning method is mentioned. Synthetic DAS counts as DAS used.

title: Reconstruction of Nearshore Surface Gravity Wave Heights From Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: The study analyzes real seafloor DAS strain recordings against a colocated pressure sensor. It relies on linear correlation and an analytical transfer function from wave theory; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Supervised Deep Learning for Detecting and Locating Passive Seismic Events Recorded with DAS: A Case Study
rationale: Authors train a supervised deep neural network to detect and locate passive seismic events recorded with DAS. Training used synthetic data mixed with real noise, and testing used an Otway field dataset, so the data are not simulated only.

title: Maximize the value of DAS VSP using full wavefields
rationale: The abstract applies dynamic matching FWI and reverse time migration to DAS VSP data, with no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central, and DAS data are analyzed; whether those data are field or synthetic is not stated.

title: Diverse applications of DAS and their added values: A case study from Minami-aga pilot CCUS project, onshore Japan
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning. It describes field DAS deployments at the Minami-aga CCUS pilot for VSP, crosswell seismic, microseismic monitoring and injection profiling, which is observed elastic-wave data.

title: Comparison of straight and helical fibers for time-lapse elastic FWI of synthetic seafloor DAS data
rationale: Elastic full-waveform inversion is a physics-based iterative inversion; no machine learning is mentioned. The analysis uses synthetic seafloor DAS data from straight and helical fibers, so DAS is used and all data are simulated.

title: Evaluating distributed acoustic sensing for crosswell seismic surveys with helical and linear fibers using conventional P-, SH-, and SV-wave sources
rationale: Field crosswell surveys at Svelvik recorded on helical and linear DAS fibers with active P, SH, SV sources, compared with conventional sensors; no machine learning mentioned, only signal-to-noise and arrival-time comparisons.

title: Urban site characterization using DAS dark fibers on the MIT campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts
rationale: Field DAS experiment on campus dark fibers; ambient Rayleigh-wave dispersion is inverted for shear-wave velocity profiles using conventional inversion and site-response modeling. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Detection of microseismic events in continuous DAS recordings using semantic image segmentation
rationale: The authors train a semantic image segmentation model on synthetic DAS strain data, then apply it to field DAS recordings from hydraulic fracturing. Segmentation models of this kind are implicitly neural networks, so the family is deep learning.

title: Seismic monitoring of CCS with active and passive data: A synthetic feasibility study based on Pelican site, Australia
rationale: Uses full waveform inversion and wave-equation dispersion inversion, which are physics-based methods with no machine learning. The analysis is applied to synthetic seafloor DAS strain and displacement datasets, so all data are simulated.

title: Measurement of ocean currents by seafloor distributed optical-fiber acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS data from a seafloor fiber cable analyzed with ambient-noise interferometry, beamforming and waveform stretching; no machine learning mentioned. Ocean buoy observations used for validation.

title: Learning Gradient Descent to Optimize DAS Signal Estimation
rationale: Authors build neural network optimization units to emulate MAP denoising for downhole DAS signals, tested on synthetic and field DAS data, so DAS is used and the AI role is methodological deep learning.

title: Monitoring Slug Flow Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Technology with Different Sensing Cable Configurations
rationale: Experimental DAS recordings of slug flow in a pipeline, analyzed with standard deviation downsampling, frequency estimation and semblance velocity analysis; no machine learning is mentioned. DAS senses acoustic/strain-rate signals, so the family is seismic_elastic.

title: Quantum weak measurement enhanced distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work uses interferometry and a Fourier transform. DAS is central, but the abstract offers only theoretical analysis of a proposed scheme, with no stated measured or simulated data.

title: Comparison of the Sensitivity of Various Fibers in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Laboratory experimental comparison of seven fibers' acoustic sensitivity in a DAS setup; amplitude-frequency responses measured. No machine learning mentioned. DAS data acquired and analyzed directly.

title: A Sensitive Frequency Band Study for Distributed Acoustical Sensing Monitoring Based on the Coupled Simulation of Gas–Liquid Two-Phase Flow and Acoustic Processes
rationale: Physics-based coupled flow-acoustic simulation with no machine learning mentioned. Oil field DAS acoustic data are analyzed to identify sensitive frequency bands, so DAS is used on observed field data.

title: High-resolution geophysical monitoring of moisture accumulation preceding slope movement—a path to improved early warning
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning; field ERT and low-frequency DAS strain measurements are analyzed jointly, with auxiliary hydrological and slope displacement data, on a real clay slope.

title: Removing Instrumental Noise in Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data: A Comparison Between Two Deep Learning Approaches
rationale: Authors train neural networks (supervised and Noise2Noise) to denoise DAS data, using real interrogator noise recorded on an isolated coil plus synthetic data, and real downhole fiber recordings.

title: Distributed fiber-optic temperature monitoring in boreholes of a seasonal geothermal energy storage
other_family_note: distributed fiber-optic temperature sensing (DTS) in boreholes
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned. The cable supports DAS, but the paper's analysis focuses on DTS temperature data recorded during cementation, so DAS data are not analyzed.

title: Classification of images derived from submarine fibre optic sensing: detecting broadband seismic activity from hydroacoustic signals
rationale: Authors train a 2-D CNN classifier, with Gaussian process hyperparameter tuning, on field DAS recordings from a 55-km ocean-bottom cable off Cape Muroto to separate seismic, other hydroacoustic and noise images.

title: Frequency-modulated dual-pulse phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometry with direct detection
Metasurface-Enhanced Fiber-Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: There is no machine learning; the work designs an acoustic metasurface lens. Its DAS sensing unit is tested through simulation and experiments on a 3D-printed structure, giving roughly 10 dB sensitivity gain. DAS acoustic data are therefore analyzed.

title: Subsurface Imaging in Urban Areas With Ambient Noise Using DAS and Seismometer Data Sets: Granada, Spain
other_family_note: Legacy borehole sonic well log used to relate MHVSR peak frequencies to depth
rationale: The study analyzes a 10-hour DAS strain-rate recording from a telecom cable and nearby seismometer noise using autocorrelation and MHVSR. These are conventional methods, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Range-scalable distributed acoustic sensing with EDFA repeaters demonstrated over 2227 km
rationale: Instrumentation paper demonstrating repeatered DAS interrogation over a 2227 km fiber line with measured strain resolution; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data acquired experimentally, so das_used is yes.

title: Variable gauge length: Processing theory and applications to distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Signal-processing method for variable gauge length in DAS; no machine learning mentioned. Applied to synthetic VSP data and actual field DAS datasets, so DAS data are analyzed and not all data are simulated.

title: Field Experiments of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Measurements
rationale: Field DAS experiments on a bridge and tunnel detect vehicles, shore activity and microseisms using only filtering and normalization; no machine learning is mentioned. The DAS data are observed field measurements.

title: Estimation of shallow structure along the hinagu fault by applying seismic interferometry to DAS observations conducted along national route 3 in Kumamoto prefecture, Japan
rationale: Field DAS ambient noise recorded on a telecom fiber, processed with cross-correlation, three-station interferometry and MASW dispersion inversion; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Flow characteristics of gas and liquid in pipeline revealed by machine learning on distributed acoustic sensing data
Unsupervised Coherent Noise Removal From Seismological Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: Extends self-supervised Noise2Self denoising model (a neural-network framework, implied) to DAS data; evaluated on synthetic data from seismometer recordings and applied to a real DAS array at the Alpine Fault.

title: A data assimilation-based method for real-time monitoring and estimation of gas influx size and distribution during gas migration in a marine drilling riser
Rapid-repeat time-lapse vertical seismic profile imaging of CO2 injection
rationale: Elastic full-waveform inversion, a physics-based method with no ML mentioned, is applied to field time-lapse VSP data combining geophones and DAS, plus a synthetic validation experiment.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing System Utilizing Phase-OTDR Integrated With One-Way Ring SI via Undersampling Recovery Algorithm
rationale: The paper builds a phase-OTDR DAS system with a Sagnac interferometer and tests it on experimental vibration signals. Recovery relies on cross-correlation and frequency mapping, with no machine learning mentioned.

title: Fine-scale Southern California Moho structure uncovered with distributed acoustic sensing

title: Intelligent Traffic Monitoring with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Two CNNs are trained on synthetic DAS traffic data, combined with a Hough transform, and tested on real DAS recordings for vehicle trajectory segmentation and velocity estimation. DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: A Sensor Fusion Scheme Integrating Fiber-Optic Geophone and DAS
rationale: Hardware paper fusing DAS with fabricated fiber-optic geophones; experimental sensitivity measurements of DAS phase responses reported. No machine learning mentioned. DAS data experimentally acquired and analyzed.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) for longwall coal mines
rationale: The abstract demonstrates field DAS fiber deployments in longwall coal mines for seismic monitoring. No machine learning or AI method is mentioned; the data are observed strain/seismic measurements from DAS.

title: Detection of aircraft noise using distributed acoustic sensing with a buried telecommunication cable
rationale: The authors analyze a four-week field DAS recording from a buried telecom cable to detect acoustic signals from aircraft. No machine-learning method is mentioned; the analysis is signal-based.

title: An Event Recognition Method for a Φ-OTDR System Based on CNN-BiGRU Network Model with Attention
rationale: Authors propose a CNN-BiGRU-attention network that classifies vibration events in Φ-OTDR DAS signals. They validate it on real-world DAS data for security monitoring, so the analysis uses observed DAS measurements.

title: Downhole Microseismic Detection Using Fiber-Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on Segmentation Model and Connected Domain Algorithm
rationale: Authors build a deep segmentation model (MobileNetV3 with dynamic snake convolution, LRASPP head) and apply it to a field downhole DAS microseismic dataset from Utah, reporting F1 scores.

title: Experimental investigation of water pipeline leakage monitoring utilizing piezoelectric distributed acoustic sensing technology
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; leaks are located with a flow-velocity equation. Controlled experiments record leak vibration with a piezoelectric distributed acoustic sensing geocable. It is labelled DAS, though it is not fiber-optic.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation of DAS Amplitude and Its Implications for Earthquake Early Warning and Seismic Interferometry
rationale: The authors calibrate three field DAS arrays against co-located seismometers and evaluate amplitude, noise floor and seismic interferometry. The abstract mentions no machine learning; all data are observed seismic recordings.

title: Achievements in Volcano Research in the Earthquake and Volcano Hazards Observation and Research Program from 2019 to 2023: Towards Prediction of Volcanic Eruptions by Building Volcanic Activity Transition Models
rationale: A program-level review summarizing volcano research results, with no machine learning mentioned. It reports DAS observations used to locate volcanic earthquakes and estimate structure, alongside isotopes, tremor, seismic surveys and drone aeromagnetics.

title: The GorDAS Distributed Acoustic Sensing Experiment Above the Cascadia Locked Zone and Subducted Gorda Slab
rationale: Field DAS recordings on buried telecom fiber, checked against nodal seismometers. The detector is compared to a catalog built with deep-learning phase pickers; it is implied but not stated that the authors ran those pickers.

title: Where Is the Fluid? Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing–Based Strain Measurement in Near Real Time
rationale: Kalman filter-based inversion of low-frequency DAS strain is classical estimation, not ML. Field and theoretical examples use DAS strain data. Microseismic incorporation is mentioned only as a possibility.

title: Urban sensing using existing fiber-optic networks
other_family_note: environmental (acoustic) noise level data compared with seismic source power
rationale: A 50 km telecom fiber was repurposed as DAS to locate urban seismic sources and map source power, then correlated with noise, land use and demographics. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: To Detect Strong Nugget with an Acoustic Array
other_family_note: Acoustic signals (microphones, hydrophones/ocean acoustics) from nugget impacts, calculated
rationale: The paper presents theoretical calculations of impact acoustic and seismic signals, with no machine learning mentioned. Distributed acoustic sensing appears only as a possible future application, not as data the authors analyzed.

title: Co-wavelength-channel integration of ultra-low-frequency distributed acoustic sensing and high-capacity communication
other_family_note: fiber-optic telecom transmission signal performance (communication capacity, BER)
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; demodulation uses cross-correlation. The authors build and test a DAS system over a 38 km seven-core fiber, measuring strain sensitivity alongside telecom transmission capacity.

title: Distributed Acoustic Sensing Along a Shallow Water Energy Cable
rationale: Authors analyze field DAS recordings on an offshore tidal energy cable, observing ocean waves and vessel signals via frequency band energy plots; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Enhancing P-wave velocity model at the Utah FORGE EGS site using traveltime tomography and full-waveform inversion of 2D DAS-VSP and 3D surface seismic data
other_family_note: borehole well-log data used for validation
rationale: The study uses traveltime tomography and acoustic full-waveform inversion, which are conventional methods; no machine learning is mentioned. Field 2D DAS-VSP data are directly inverted alongside 3D surface seismic, and results are validated against well logs.

title: Velocity Model Calibration Based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing Perforation Data
rationale: Velocity calibration uses travel-time inversion with particle swarm optimization, a global optimizer rather than machine learning. The method is tested on synthetic data, then applied to real DAS perforation arrival times, with sonic logs defining layers.

title: Phase Unwrapping Algorithm for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Based on Unlimited Sampling and Phase Diversity
rationale: Signal-processing phase unwrapping (unlimited sampling, phase diversity) with no machine learning; applied to laboratory DAS strain data generated by a fiber stretcher per SEAFOM guidelines, so DAS is used on observed lab data.

title: Estimating sound pressure levels from distributed acoustic sensing data using 20 Hz fin whale calls
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the strain-to-pressure conversion is physics-based. Field DAS recordings of fin whale calls from three seafloor telecom cable deployments are analyzed directly.

title: KVP: a multiscale kurtosis approach for seismic phase picking
rationale: The core picker is kurtosis-based, not ML, but the authors run PhaseNet, a deep-learning picker, on their data as a benchmark. Earthquake DAS recordings from land and submarine fibres, plus OBS data, are analyzed directly.

title: Complex principal component analysis of volcanic earthquakes at Azuma volcano, Japan, recorded by a distributed acoustic sensing system (DAS) for the hypocenter determination
rationale: Field DAS recordings of volcanic earthquakes at Azuma are analyzed with complex PCA, cross-spectral arrival-time measurement and relative hypocenter location. These are conventional methods, so no ML is used.

title: Damage state monitoring of buried pipeline based on distributed acoustic sensing technology
Local earthquake response on the submarine communication cable in the northern South China Sea
rationale: Authors analyze observed DAS recordings of ten local earthquakes on a submarine telecom cable and denoise them with stacking, wavelet transform and empirical mode decomposition. These are conventional signal processing, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Imaging Processing of 3D DAS‐VSP Data Jointly Acquired With a High‐Density OBN Survey in the Middle East
rationale: The workflow is conventional DAS-VSP processing: deblending, ringing-noise removal, full waveform inversion and wave-equation migration. No ML is mentioned. Field 3D DAS-VSP data from 13 wells were imaged alongside OBN seismic.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing in harsh environments based on femtosecond laser-inscribed ultra-short fiber Bragg grating arrays
rationale: The authors build and test a DAS system (USFBG arrays with phi-OTDR), measuring strain resolution in laboratory demonstrations. Pulse compression is signal processing, not machine learning, and no ML is mentioned.

title: Marine Seismic Exploration with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; the paper presents a DAS-based fiber-optic towed streamer system validated with field sea-trial marine seismic data, so DAS data were analyzed.

title: Acoustic Events Detection and Classification for Urban DAS Data with Supervised Learning
rationale: Authors develop a deep learning detector and classifier trained on annotated field DAS recordings from an urban array in Tangshan, classifying earthquakes, vehicles, traffic and industrial vibrations.

title: Evaluating the performance of distributed acoustic sensing for crosswell seismic imaging of abandoned mine geothermal systems
rationale: Field crosswell active-source survey recorded with DAS and a colocated hydrophone array; first arrivals and coda are analyzed, with no machine learning mentioned. DTS appears only as the fiber's original purpose, not as analyzed data.

title: Wellbore fluid flow velocity calculation based on distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: The authors combine cross-correlation with a clustering step (unsupervised classical ML) to estimate wellbore flow velocities. The method is checked on actual DAS recordings of flow-induced acoustic noise, so DAS is used on observed data.

title: Monitoring bands during the Norwegian national day parade: a case study on urban distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS recordings on urban dark fiber in Oslo were analyzed for band detection using harmonic frequency characteristics and speed estimation; no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Characterizing Vehicle-Induced Distributed Acoustic Sensing Signals for Accurate Urban Near-Surface Imaging
rationale: Field DAS records from roadside telecom fiber are analyzed. Vehicles are grouped by amplitude and arrival-time thresholds, and surface-wave dispersion is inverted. No machine-learning model is mentioned.

title: Machine learning generated solitons for distributed acoustic sensing
other_family_note: optical soliton pulse propagation in fiber (interrogator pulse design), not sensed acoustic data
rationale: The authors use machine learning techniques to design long-duration solitons, an applied method with an unstated model family. DAS is the target application, but the abstract never says whether any DAS or fiber data were analyzed.

title: Research on the mechanism of LF-DAS fiber-optic strain rate evolution and automatic interpretation method for multivariate monitoring wells
A DAS Monitoring System for Underground Cables Using Multi-Scale Dynamic Mel Frequency Cepstral Features
rationale: Features extracted from DAS vibration signals on buried cables feed a neural network that classifies eight event types; the experiments apply real vibrations, so the data are observed, not simulated.

title: Minute-scale dynamics of recurrent dike intrusions in Iceland with fiber-optic geodesy
rationale: Low-frequency DAS strain recorded on a telecom fiber near Grindavík is inverted geodetically to image dike intrusions. The abstract mentions no machine learning; the inversion is a conventional geodetic method.

title: Research on MSC-ANC noise reduction analysis for wire break signal monitoring in prestressed concrete cylinder pipe
rationale: Authors apply a convolutional autoencoder with an SE-network for denoising and a k-nearest neighbors classifier to DAS wire-break signals from PCCP pipes, evaluated through experiments. The DAS-sensed acoustic field counts as seismic_elastic.

title: An analysis of the dynamic range of Distributed Acoustic Sensing for Earthquake Early Warning
rationale: Theoretical and practical analysis of DAS dynamic range with an information-content method; no machine learning mentioned. Methods applied to observed DAS recordings from offshore Chile.

title: Marine Soundscape Monitoring Enabled by Artificial Intelligence-Aided Integrated Distributed Sensing and Communications
other_family_note: fiber-optic telecom traffic (communication signal SNR/BER measurements); underwater acoustics sensed by DAS
rationale: Authors apply a CNN to classify marine animal sounds sensed by DAS on telecom fiber, both in a water tank and in the Red Sea. They also measure communication performance over the same fiber.

title: Real-time distributed acoustic sensing based on phase-sensitive optical time-domain reflectometer with fading suppression
rationale: Hardware and signal-processing paper on a phase-OTDR DAS system with fading suppression and FPGA demodulation; no machine learning mentioned. Laboratory and field vibration experiments use DAS data, so DAS use is yes.

title: Monitoring and strengthening of prestressed concrete cylinder pipes based on distributed acoustic sensing and iron-based shape memory alloys
other_family_note: laboratory mechanical testing: strain and crack measurements on concrete pipe
rationale: A full-scale pipe test used DAS to detect wire-break acoustic signals, so DAS is used and counts as elastic/acoustic sensing. Mechanical strain and crack tests are added as other. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Distributed acoustic sensing with high response bandwidth and large dynamic range using multi-frequency time-slot multiplexing pulses based on UWFBG array
Forward Modeling of Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing Optical Fiber Strain and Strain-Rate Patterns Induced by 3D Complex Fractures in Horizontal Wells
rationale: The paper uses physics-based displacement discontinuity simulation of LF-DAS strain, with no machine learning mentioned. Simulated patterns are compared against field LF-DAS monitoring data from Sichuan Basin shale gas fracturing, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Automatic Identification of Diverse Tunnel Threats With Machine Learning–Based Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Authors train a stacking ensemble learning model and anomaly detection pipeline on a DAS fiber-optic vibroacoustic dataset of tunnel events, applied in a real tunnel; DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Rail track support condition monitoring with distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) system
rationale: Field test with a rail-mounted DAS cable measuring rail strain under locomotive loading. No machine learning or AI is mentioned. The DAS strain data were observed in the field, with support changes made physically by removing crossties.

title: Lightweight fiber optic intrusion detection system
Elastic full-waveform inversion: Enhance imaging for legacy and modern acquisition
rationale: Physics-based acoustic and elastic FWI with no machine learning mentioned. FWI is applied to acquired data, including a DAS-VSP survey alongside node and narrow-azimuth seismic data, so DAS data are analyzed.

title: Uncertainty quantification in elastic full-waveform inversion as a means to access complementary aspects in DAS and accelerometer data
rationale: Elastic FWI is run through a recurrent neural network framework on field data from the Snowflake VSP, which has fiber-optic DAS and accelerometers. The RNN may be a physics-based wave formulation rather than a learned model.

title: High-sensitivity simultaneously distributed acoustic and temperature sensing by an air-ring microstructured optical fiber
other_family_note: distributed temperature sensing by optical fiber
rationale: Abstract describes a new microstructured fiber for DAS, with measured acoustic and temperature sensitivities; no machine learning mentioned. The DAS data are the authors' own experimental measurements, plus fiber-based temperature sensing.

title: Estimating Focal Mechanism of Small Earthquakes Using S/P Amplitude Ratios of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Records
rationale: Grid search over focal mechanism parameters using S/P amplitude ratios from DAS records of four real Japanese earthquakes, compared with seismometer polarities; no machine learning mentioned.

title: Method to Use Transport Microsimulation Models to Create Synthetic Distributed Acoustic Sensing Datasets
rationale: Authors train U-Net CNNs on synthetic DAS traffic signals for resolution enhancement and directional filtering, then apply them to real DAS measurements from a road test site, so the data are not purely simulated.

title: Field-Measured Vehicle Signal Comparison with Modeled Response of Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning; it uses an analytical Flamant-Boussinesq model of the DAS strain response. The title implies comparison with field-measured vehicle DAS signals, so DAS was used and the data are not only simulated.

title: Reservoir properties estimation before and after hydraulic stimulation using extended elastic full-waveform inversion and distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: The authors apply elastic full-waveform inversion, a physics-based method with no machine learning, to a field DAS dataset recorded from perforation shots. DAS data are therefore directly analyzed, and the data are observed rather than simulated.

title: Urban traffic monitoring through Distributed Acoustic Sensing: Trial analysis of a potent monitoring tool
rationale: The authors apply clustering techniques (unsupervised classical ML) to field DAS recordings of urban traffic in Granada. These data are used to study feature selection and separability of the traffic events.

title: Exploration of Perimeter Security Intrusion Recognition Method Based on DAS and GASF-MSCNN
rationale: Authors train a multi-scale CNN on GASF images built from DAS fiber vibration signals collected for five intrusion event types, comparing against CNN, LSTM and TCN. DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Xdas: A Python Framework for Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Software description of a Python library for DAS data handling; no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central, but the abstract states no specific data analysis, so das_used is unclear.

title: Enhancing fin whale vocalizations in distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: Observed OOI cable DAS data are analyzed with matched filtering, Gabor filtering, SNR estimation and envelope subtraction. These are conventional signal processing, with no machine learning mentioned, so AI role is none and DAS is used.

title: Dual-Domain SNR Enhancement and Fading Suppression Method for ϕ-OTDR
rationale: The signal processing uses moving averages and a DCT non-local means filter, with no machine learning. DAS data come from an experimental phi-OTDR system on a 6 km fiber.

title: Rapid Diagnosis of Distributed Acoustic Sensing Vibration Signals Using Mel-Frequency Cepstral Coefficients and Liquid Neural Networks
rationale: Liquid neural networks are trained to classify DAS vibration signals, compared with 1D-CNN and LSTM baselines. Validation uses simulated data and real DAS data from a port conveyor belt, so DAS is used and the data are not simulated-only.

title: Rapid and Temporary Deployment of Fiber-Optic Arrays to Measure Surface Chemical Explosion Series with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS campaigns recording explosion seismoacoustic waves, validated against geophones, with anemometers for wind; no machine learning mentioned, so ai_role is none, and observed DAS data were analyzed.

title: Transdimensional surface wave inversion of the near surface: Application to distributed acoustic sensing data
rationale: Bayesian transdimensional MCMC inversion (birth-death, Gibbs sampler) is not machine learning. Field active-source DAS strain-rate surface waves from Groningen are analyzed; borehole S-wave logs are used as prior and validation, still seismic velocity.

title: Hardware-Efficient Phase Demodulation for Digital ϕ-OTDR Receivers with Baseband and Analytic Signal Processing
rationale: The paper uses signal processing (zero-IF, Hilbert, wavelet transforms, phase unwrapping) with no machine learning. The methods are evaluated on simulated and real phi-OTDR DAS data, explicitly framed as DAS demodulator design.

title: Integrated and adaptive monitoring of geological carbon storage operations with surface distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Surface DAS monitoring concept tested in a digital twin of a North Sea aquifer (simulated seismic data); no machine learning mentioned. DAS is central and analyzed via simulated experiments.

title: Unsupervised Weak Speech Enhancement Using Periodic Mixing Invariant Training
Enhanced P-wave velocity imaging by marine airgun-source seismic surveys with distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field airgun survey off Sanriku recorded with seafloor DAS cable and OBSs; refraction tomography for Vp imaging, compared with reflection profile. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Pre-existing concrete pipe disconnection detection based on fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing
Intelligent Vehicle Automatic Identification and Classification With Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors build a GAN-based denoiser and apply a YOLOv8 segmentation model to urban dark-fiber DAS field data from Changchun to classify vehicles and estimate speeds. DAS vibration counts as seismic_elastic.

title: A review of seismic detection using fiber optic distributed acoustic sensing: from telecommunication cables to earthquake sensors
Evaluating subsurface imaging performance with ocean-bottom distributed acoustic sensing and double beamforming
rationale: Observed ocean-bottom DAS data from a 60-km Oregon cable are analyzed with ambient-noise cross-correlation, double beamforming and perturbational inversion. These are conventional methods, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: Vehicle vibration signal classification for ultra-weak fiber Bragg grating distributed acoustic sensing systems
rationale: Seven ML algorithms (BP neural network, KNN, AdaBoost, random forest, CNN) classify vehicle vibration signals collected by a buried-cable uwDAS platform and public DAS data, so DAS is used and ML is the method.

title: Zero-Shot Denoising for DAS-VSP Data Based on Conditional Diffusion Probabilistic Models
rationale: Authors build a conditional diffusion model with dilated convolutions to denoise DAS-VSP data, tested on synthetic and real seismic datasets; DAS is the analyzed data.

title: USING DISTRIBUTED FIBER-OPTIC SENSING TO RECORD SANDBAR MIGRATION UNDER CALM AND ENERGETIC CONDITIONS
other_family_note: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) along fiber-optic cable
rationale: Authors present field observations from combined DAS and DTS in a nearshore setting, relating strain, temperature and cable burial; no machine learning or AI method is mentioned.

title: Integrated ultra-large dynamic vibration sensing with fronthaul analog radio-over-fiber transmission
rationale: No machine learning mentioned; pulse compression and waveform design only. Authors experimentally demonstrate frequency-demodulated DAS measuring vibration strain along a 10-km fiber in an integrated sensing-communication fronthaul system.

title: Approach Interprets Fracture Growth Through Microseismic Quiescent Zones
other_family_note: well pressure observations during hydraulic fracturing
rationale: No machine learning is mentioned; the work integrates microseismic monitoring, low-frequency DAS strain, pressure, tiltmeters and geochemical fingerprinting of produced oils. The Uinta Basin case study analyzes field DAS data.

title: Endogenous integration of communication and interference fading free sensing using telecom pilots via joint polarization-fraction domain multiplexing
other_family_note: fiber-optic telecom signals (polarization rotation monitoring, coherent transmission)
rationale: The work uses fractional Fourier transform signal processing with no machine learning. An experimental DAS measures vibrations over 10.4 km of fiber alongside coherent telecom transmission and SOP monitoring.

title: A VMD-LMS filtering approach for DAS noise suppression
rationale: Denoising relies on variational mode decomposition plus adaptive LMS filtering, which is conventional signal processing, not machine learning. DAS signals are analyzed in both simulations and experiments over a roughly 97 km sensing range.

title: A Novel SNR Enhancement Method for Complex Multimode Signals in ϕ-OTDR Systems Using SVMD and Shifting Window Pearson Correlation Coefficient
rationale: The denoising relies on variational mode decomposition and windowed Pearson correlation, which are signal processing, not ML. Experimental Φ-OTDR/DAS signals were acquired, including from field seismic experiments and sledgehammer impact tests.

title: Borehole Seismic Monitoring of a Rock Massif Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing on an Undermined Territory
rationale: Field DAS cross-well seismic monitoring with an active borehole source at a salt deposit; wave fields are compared to locate elastic changes. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Research Progress on Vehicle Status Information Perception Based on Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Review of DAS-based vehicle perception; deep learning is discussed as one surveyed algorithm class rather than applied by the authors. DAS is central, but it is unclear whether the authors analyzed data themselves.

title: Exploring Research Trends in Distributed Acoustic Sensing with Machine Learning and Deep Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis of Themes and Emerging Topics
rationale: A bibliometric review of Scopus publications on ML/DL in DAS. No model is applied to data and no DAS measurements are analyzed. DAS and AI are only the topic of the literature survey.

title: Directional sensitivity of fibre optic cables for surface seismic reflection distributed acoustic sensing: a review and potential solutions for enhanced sensitivity
rationale: The abstract mentions no machine learning. It is a review of DAS cable designs for surface seismic reflection. DAS is central, but the abstract does not say whether the authors analyzed any DAS data themselves.

title: Leakage diagnosis method of injection-production string in underground gas storage wellbore based on cooperative monitoring of multi-physical fields
Fiber‐Seismometer Hybrid Sensing Interferometry: A New Approach to Seismic Imaging and Monitoring
rationale: The method relies on two-step cross-correlation interferometry with no machine learning mentioned. DAS and seismometer field data near the Qiantang River are analyzed for Green's functions, dispersion, HVSR and velocity monitoring.

title: Mechanically coupled distributed dynamic strain measurement for track systems and earthworks
other_family_note: pressure sensors measuring trackbed load pressure
rationale: A ϕ-OTDR DAS system recorded dynamic strain from passing trains, compared with accelerometers, pressure sensors and simulation. No machine learning is mentioned; the analysis is conventional comparison with numerical simulation.

title: Systematic review of fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing: advancements, applications, and challenges
Hybrid multi-resolution network for DAS data denoising
rationale: Authors propose and train a multi-resolution neural network to denoise DAS seismic records, using real DAS noise plus synthetic data, and validate on actual DAS records, so observed data are included.

title: High Resolution Shallow Structure of Ebao Basin Revealed With DAS Ambient Noise Tomography and Its Relation to Earthquake Ground Motion
rationale: The authors recorded ambient noise and earthquakes on a field DAS array over a telecom fiber, then applied cross-correlation, Frequency-Bessel dispersion measurement and surface wave tomography. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: Acquisition and imaging of ocean-bottom fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing data using a full-shot carpet from a conventional 3D survey
rationale: Offshore Norway controlled-source experiment records seabed fiber DAS data, compares it with towed-streamer seismic, and performs conventional imaging. No machine learning is mentioned; the DAS data are field observations.

title: Geophysical Survey and Monitoring of Transportation Infrastructure Slopes (TISs): A Review
rationale: A literature review of geophysical slope monitoring with no analysis of its own. AI appears only as a promising future technology, with no model applied. DAS is listed among emerging technologies, not as data analyzed.

title: Integration of multi-domain das data analysis and machine learning for wellbore flow regimes identification in shale gas reservoirs
Vehicle Trajectory Extraction From Weak and Discontinuous Quasi-Static DAS Signals Using a Multiscale Context Pix2pix
rationale: Authors apply a Pix2pix GAN with dilated convolutions to field DAS quasi-static vehicle signals from campus experiments to reconstruct trajectories; DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: Optimization of passive seismic monitoring network for CO2 sequestration in Saudi Arabia
Full-waveform inversion using deviated well distributed acoustic sensing vertical seismic profiling data: A case study
rationale: The study applies conventional full-waveform inversion, with no machine learning mentioned, to field DAS VSP data recorded in an offshore deviated well. That makes AI role none and DAS used yes, from observed rather than simulated data.

title: Continuous surface distributed acoustic sensing for subsurface hydraulic fracturing source localization and near-surface scatterer imaging: A case study in the Caojiatan Mine
rationale: Field surface DAS recordings of hydraulic fracturing at a mine are processed with physical denoising, time reversal mirrors and natural migration. No machine learning is mentioned, so AI role is none and DAS is used.

title: Manipulation of Acoustic Focusing for Multi-target Sensing with Distributed Microphones in Smart Car Cabin
other_family_note: Active airborne acoustic sensing with in-cabin speakers and microphones
rationale: Uses a beamforming model and dual-frequency signals, with no machine learning mentioned. The phrase 'distributed acoustic sensing' refers to distributed microphones, not fiber-optic DAS. Real car experiments were conducted.

title: Geoscience Visual Presentation G03: Integrated and adaptive monitoring of geological carbon storage operations with surface distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Surface DAS monitoring concept tested in a digital twin of a saline aquifer (simulated seismic/DAS data); no machine learning mentioned. Ambient noise interferometry noted only as an opportunity.

title: Constraining water dynamics through unsaturated and saturated zones using fiber-optic seismic sensing data
A Method for Data Denoising and Smoothing Based on DAS VSP
rationale: Authors propose a multi-scale residual attention neural network for denoising and smoothing DAS VSP seismic data. They evaluate it on simulated and field DAS recordings, so DAS is used and the data are not simulation-only.

title: Enhancing fracture geometry monitoring in hydraulic fracturing using radial basis functions and distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Radial basis functions serve as a low-dimensional parameterization inside a physics-based inversion, not a learned ML predictor. DAS measurements from a synthetic benchmark and real field test-site data are inverted for fracture width.

title: Stress field inversion using downhole fiber-optic distributed acoustic sensing array during hydraulic fracturing in shale gas reservoir
rationale: Field downhole DAS array records microseismicity during fracturing; events located by migration, followed by moment tensor, stress inversion and focal mechanism tomography. No machine-learning method is mentioned.

title: Validation of Taylor’s Frozen Hypothesis for DAS-Based Flow
rationale: The analysis uses LES simulation, a cross-correlation template algorithm and signal denoising, with no machine learning. An experimental pipeline DAS measurement system supplied observed data to validate flow velocity, so DAS counts as an acoustic field.

title: Combining DAS Ambient Seismic Noise Interferometry and Unsupervised Machine Learning for 2D Imaging of an Urban Subsurface
rationale: Authors apply unsupervised clustering to virtual shot gathers from 15 days of field DAS data on a Berlin dark fiber, plus synthetic tests. Clustering is classical ML; surface-wave imaging is seismic.

title: Freshwater Thin Ice Sheet Monitoring and Imaging with Fiber Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing
other_family_note: ice auger thickness measurements used for validation
rationale: Field DAS deployments on frozen ponds analyzed via phase velocity transformations of strike tests; no machine learning mentioned. Ice auger thickness checks used for validation.

title: Low-Frequency Distributed Acoustic Sensing Monitoring during Subsea Oilwell Startup: A North Sea Case Study
rationale: This is a field case study interpreting real-time low-frequency DAS from a North Sea subsea well during startup. No machine learning is mentioned. LF-DAS strain data is coded as seismic_elastic per the DAS rule.

title: On the variation of ocean surface gravity wave characteristics with wind speed and direction: a case study from offshore Svalbard, Norway
rationale: Long-term DAS recordings on two Svalbard fibre segments are analysed for ocean wave arrival angles and swell properties. No machine learning is mentioned. Local wind direction data are implied but not detailed.

title: Real-Time Railway Hazard Detection Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Hybrid Ensemble Learning
rationale: Authors train SVM, random forest, boosting and a voting ensemble to classify vibrations recorded by DAS fiber along a 6 km Turkish railway corridor, with real-world detection results reported.

title: Non-local self-similarity guided graph attention network for DAS-VSP noise and signal separation
Applying Machine Learning and Bayesian Inference to Identify and Locate Moving Anthropogenic Sources Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data
rationale: Authors evaluate k-NN, CNN and recurrent-convolutional networks for classifying anthropogenic sources in recorded DAS data from urban telecom fibers; Kalman filtering is used for locating them. The DAS data appear to be observed.

title: Ocean Observations Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing with a 29 km long Submarine Cable in the Northern South China Sea
rationale: Field DAS data from a 29 km submarine cable record earthquakes, ocean waves and microseisms. Results are compared with wave/current meter and anemometer observations. No machine learning is mentioned; analysis relies on spectrograms.

title: Subsurface Imaging in Urban Environments: Utilizing Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Downtown Reno, Nevada
rationale: The authors process seven days of DAS ambient noise from a dark-fiber line using interferometry and dispersion analysis to build a shear-wave velocity model. They validate it against existing microgravity data. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: A comprehensive experimental assessment of reinforced concrete walls under blast: In situ monitoring of loading, dynamic response and damage with NDT methods and embedded sensors
other_family_note: Blast pressure sensors, distributed fiber-optic strain sensing (DSS), ultrasound structure scanning of concrete
rationale: An experimental blast-test study using pressure sensors, DIC, accelerometers, embedded fiber-optic DAS for internal dynamics, DSS and ultrasound. Numerical blast simulations are included, but no machine learning is mentioned.

title: A multitask deep-learning model for the denoising, interpolation, and wavefield separation of distributed acoustic sensing-vertical seismic profiling data
rationale: Authors build and train a hybrid CNN-transformer model for denoising, interpolation and wavefield separation, tested on synthetic and field DAS-VSP records, so DAS data are analyzed and observed data are included.

title: Observations of fin whales and vessels offshore oregon using fibre optic distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS data from an Oregon submarine cable were analysed with template matching, correlation, stacking and conventional location methods. No machine learning is mentioned, so ai_role is none and das_used is yes.

title: Breaking Through the Frequency Response Limit in DAS Using UWFBG Arrays and DSTDM Method
rationale: DAS hardware/interrogation paper using UWFBG arrays and dual-stage time-division multiplexing; experimental vibration sensing results reported. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Subsurface structure assessment for landfill using distributed acoustic sensing: A case study in Qingdao, China
Explainable Riemannian Manifold Learning for Application Scene Generalization With Distributed Acoustic Sensing System
rationale: Authors propose and field-test a Riemannian transformer deep-learning classifier on DAS intrusion-event data from subway construction and gas pipeline monitoring. DAS vibration sensing counts as seismic_elastic.

title: An Analysis of Railway Activity Using Distributed Optical Fiber Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS data were acquired along 12 km of railway and used to train machine learning models that detect and classify intrusion events. The model family is not specified, so it is marked uncertain.

title: Characterizing Fractured Zones in Urban Karst Geology Using Leaky Surface Waves From Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The workflow uses ambient noise interferometry, F-K filtering, stacking, dispersion inversion and rock physics modeling, with no machine learning mentioned. The authors analyze traffic noise recorded by DAS on existing urban telecom fiber.

title: Imaging the Sediment Cover Offshore Central Chile With Surface‐Wave Dispersion and P‐Wave Conversion Using Distributed Acoustic Sensing

rationale: The authors used field LF-DAS fiber monitoring and downhole camera imaging to evaluate cluster fluid and sand distribution, then ran a coupled numerical model. No machine learning is mentioned.

title: A Systematic and Comprehensive Review on the Application of the Distributed Acoustic Sensing Data in Subsurface Application: Methodologies, Deep Learning Approaches, and Future Prospects
rationale: Systematic literature review of DAS processing and deep learning (CNNs) across 149 studies; authors do not apply models or analyze DAS data themselves, so AI is the subject and DAS data are not analyzed.

title: Binary-Tree Structure for Extended Range-Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Hardware paper proposing a binary-tree DAS architecture, with on-site field testing detecting vibrations over a 10 km link. No machine learning is mentioned; the authors analyzed DAS vibration data themselves.

title: Investigation of stress wave velocity imaging in cross-sea bridge pile foundation based on DAS technology
Soil slope monitoring with Distributed Acoustic Sensing under wetting and drying cycles
rationale: Field DAS monitoring of a soil slope using ambient noise interferometry and nanostrain analysis, combined with in situ soil moisture measurements. No machine learning is mentioned; the data are observed field records.

title: Risk-based framework for Compliance Assessment and CO₂ Geological Storage Monitoring: Application in the Getica CCS Study
rationale: The paper describes a risk-based monitoring plan for CO2 storage and mentions no machine learning. DAS-based 4D seismic is one planned technology among many. No analyzed DAS or other measurement data is stated.

title: DAS-MAE: A Self-Supervised Framework for Universal and High-Performance Representation Learning of Distributed Acoustic Sensing

title: Large CP-ϕOTDR for Quasi-Static to Single-Shot Nanostrain Measurements With High Dynamic Range

title: Deep Learning-Based Blind Denoising for Distributed Acoustic Sensing Seismic Data With Self-Supervised and Transfer Learning

title: Compensation of laser source frequency drift in Φ-OTDR system using inter-pulse difference
rationale: Signal-processing method (inter-pulse differencing) for laser drift compensation in a COTDR DAS system, validated experimentally on vibration signals; no machine learning mentioned. DAS data analyzed experimentally.

title: Numerical Modeling of ϕ -OTDR Using UWFBG Array and Pulse Compression: Crosstalk Analysis and Phase Noise Compensation in Space- and Time-Division Multiplexing Architectures
rationale: Numerical model of phi-OTDR DAS with UWFBG arrays and phase noise compensation; experimental validation implies observed DAS data. No machine learning mentioned.

title: Adaptive Noise Canceller Based on Improved Affine Projection Algorithm
DAS-Accelerometer Data Fusion With Semi-Supervised Graph Variational Autoencoder for In-Service Train Wheel Flat Detection

title: Rapid Phase Demodulation on Enhanced Frequency Channel for Single-Shot Distributed Acoustic Sensing

title: Near‐Field Acoustic Imaging Using Fiber‐Optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing and Beamforming Techniques
rationale: The method relies on beamforming and near-field array processing with no machine learning. It combines DAS channel measurements and selects high-quality channels, implying DAS data were analyzed, though the abstract never says whether the data were field or synthetic.

title: Shape self-calibration method of the distributed acoustic sensing cable for beamforming enhancement
Repositioning Submarine Communication Cables Using Ship Waves Based on Integrated Sensing and Communication Network

title: A time–space and frequency–wavenumber dual-domain fusion network for coupling noise separation

title: An Enhanced Workflow for Quantitative Evaluation of Fluid and Proppant Distribution in Multistage Fracture Treatment with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Workflow uses frequency band energy from field DAS data and a power-law model linking acoustic energy to flow rate; no machine learning is mentioned. Field applications confirm observed DAS data.

title: Phase correction based measurement enhancement for Φ-OTDR under noisy conditions
Estimating the low-frequency seismic response of submarine fiber optics with a teleseismic recording
rationale: The authors compare a teleseismic recording from a submarine DAS array with broadband seismometers using cross-correlation and dispersion analysis. No machine learning is mentioned, and the DAS data are observed field records.

title: Seismic monitoring and site responses of the 2025 Ms 6.8 Dingri earthquake using distributed acoustic sensing
rationale: Field DAS recordings of the mainshock, aftershocks and ambient noise were analyzed with spectral ratio source inversion and MASW; these are conventional methods, and no machine learning is mentioned.

title: A passive bidirectional audio transmission system with integrated sensing, energy supply, and communication
Shallow Tremors Near the Nankai Trough Activated After the M 7.6 Noto Peninsula Earthquake
rationale: Tremors observed with DAS and the DONET offshore seismic network were located by envelope correlation and amplitude attenuation; no machine learning is mentioned. Field DAS data are analyzed directly.

title: Advancing dam health monitoring with high-resolution Fiber-optic Distributed Acoustic Sensing
Seismic activities at Kikai Caldera, Japan, detected using distributed acoustic sensing via seafloor telecommunication cables
rationale: Authors recorded seafloor DAS strain on telecom cables near Kikai Caldera and located earthquakes by envelope semblance analysis; no machine learning is mentioned, and the data are observed field recordings.

title: A Semantic Representation Framework for Diverse DAS Noise Suppression Using Spatially Adaptive Discriminative GAN

Weight fusion adversarial network based on the self-collaborative strategy for denoising DAS-VSP records

rationale: Literature review of carbon storage site selection and monitoring; no machine learning mentioned. DAS, seismic, ERT, InSAR are discussed as reviewed technologies, not analyzed as the authors' own data.

title: Flow path interpretation from DAS moment tensors applied to the Enhanced Geothermal System at Utah FORGE
rationale: The authors run moment tensor inversion on microseismic events recorded by two DAS arrays in wells at Utah FORGE. No machine learning is mentioned, and the data are observed field recordings.

title: Phenomenology of Avalanche Recordings From Distributed Acoustic Sensing
Monitoring Spatiotemporal Seismic Velocity Changes Using Seismic Interferometry and Distributed Acoustic Sensing in Mexico City

title: A River on Fiber: Spatially Continuous Fluvial Monitoring with Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: Field DAS strain-rate recordings along a submerged cable in a creek, analyzed with power spectra, travel-time analysis and modeling. No machine learning is mentioned.

Listening to whales and earthquakes: on exploring hydrophone recordings and Distributed Acoustic Sensing

rationale: Authors train a semi-supervised temporal convolutional network with transfer learning for earthquake detection on DAS data, reporting accuracy and SNR; whether data are field or synthetic is not stated.

rationale: A conceptual synthesis that discusses semi-supervised learning as a paradigm, with reinforcement learning as future work; no model is applied to data. DAS is discussed and illustrated from cited cases, but it is unclear whether any DAS data were analyzed.

title: Signal to Noise Ratio Performance Analysis for Vibration Detection Using Phase Sensitive OTDR in Distributed Acoustic Sensing
rationale: The authors built a phi-OTDR DAS setup and measured SNR under applied vibrations at varying pulse widths. No machine learning is mentioned. The DAS vibration data are elastic/acoustic sensing, collected experimentally.

title: Data Fusion K-Means Clustering for Seismic Signal Classification Using Integrated DAS-Geophone Sensing
rationale: Authors apply unsupervised K-Means clustering to fused DAS and geophone seismic data to classify signals; DAS data are integrated in their own analysis. Whether data are field or synthetic is not stated.

title: Towards real-time monitoring of induced microseismicity in enhanced geothermal systems
rationale: ML models produce P/S phase probabilities that are back-projected on real continuous Hengill seismic data; family not named. A DAS relative-relocation method is proposed and tested, likely on synthetic data. FORGE application is future work.

title: Audio Clarity Improvement through Likelihood-Based Evaluation and Algorithmic Tuning Methods
rationale: The framework uses genetic algorithms, particle swarm, and PID-style metaheuristic tuning, not learned ML models, and is validated only conceptually with no stated data. DAS appears only as a future application area.
